A `worktree` prevents concurrent agents from sharing one checkout; it does not\nprevent reads outside that checkout, writes elsewhere, or arbitrary egress. The coordinator's\nnetwork policy is likewise advisory because it is checked only by callers that volunteer a\ndomain.\n\ndg-07 closes the local execution gap. A shared local-process backend consumes the exact dg-06\ndecision, renders the coordinator's policy for Anthropic Sandbox Runtime (SRT), and applies the\nresult to every vendor CLI lifecycle command: synchronous invocation, asynchronous submission,\npolling, and the autopilot local-provider harness.\n\n## What Changes\n\n### Immutable execution context\n\nDispatch receives a versioned execution context containing the routing decision identifier,\nexact agent/lane identifier, isolation, dispatch mode, canonical worktree root, and provenance.\nThe enforcement layer never re-runs routing. Standalone review-panel calls that have no routed\ncontext resolve the already-landed dg-05 fallback once from the exact `agents.yaml` lane.\nRouted callers carry the complete context in phase payload v2; every adapter lifecycle method\naccepts that context explicitly instead of reconstructing it from cwd.\n\n### Coordinator-owned network-policy export and audit\n\n`NetworkPolicyService` gains an exact-agent export. It returns the active profile-specific and\nglobal rules, a closed default-deny contract, schema revision, and a deterministic digest.\nRendering is conservative: SRT denies take precedence, so conflicting authored rules may become\nnarrower but never wider. A malformed or unavailable cold-start export renders deny-all; it does\nnot invent destinations.\n\nA narrow sandbox-execution audit endpoint durably and idempotently records applied and degraded\noutcomes. If the coordinator is unavailable, a locked mode-0600 JSONL outbox under the operator's\nXDG state directory is fsynced and retried oldest-first on later calls. An unsandboxed fallback is\nallowed only after either the coordinator event or the durable outbox record succeeds.\n\n### Pure renderer and lifecycle-owning backend\n\n`skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` provides:\n\n- pure, deterministic SRT settings rendering;\n- mode-aware filesystem policy (`review` has no project write roots; write-capable modes are\n  confined to the canonical worktree root; every lane gets an ephemeral vendor-state root);\n- a prepared-command lifecycle that owns a unique mode-0600 settings file, sanitized environment,\n  runtime identity, policy digest, process group, and cleanup;\n- an additive renderer seam for future runtimes.\n\nThe reviewed runtime is `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 on Node >=20.11.0. The repository\npins the package and integrity and never installs it during dispatch. Setup/CI install the pin;\nruntime discovery is explicit absolute override, then the dispatcher's Git-root installation,\nthen unavailable. The runtime is accepted only when package metadata and integrity match. On Linux\nthe preflight also verifies `bubblewrap`, `socat`,\n`ripgrep`, user-namespace capability, architecture/seccomp support, and a real no-op SRT launch.\n\nOfficial runtime sources:\n\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/README.md\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/package.json\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-9gqj-5w7c-vx47\n\n### One local command backend\n\nThe shared backend replaces direct vendor subprocess launches in `CliVendorAdapter` sync submit,\nasync submit and poll paths, and in `autopilot/scripts/provider_dispatch.py`. Poll enforcement\nfailures are collection failures retried to the existing deadline, not terminal remote-task\nfailures. A structural guard\nprevents future vendor CLI subprocess sinks outside the backend. Non-sandbox decisions preserve\nargv, stdin, cwd, timeout, and result behavior.\n\n### Loud, bounded degradation\n\nFail-open is restricted to facts known before a vendor process starts: unsupported OS, missing or\nincompatible pinned runtime, or failed platform capability preflight. Those cases warn, durably\naudit `applied=false`, and run the original command. Unsafe roots, malformed policy, settings\nmaterialization errors, and audit/outbox failures fail closed. Once SRT starts, a timeout or\nunknown failure never triggers an unsandboxed retry because doing so could execute work twice.\n\n## Scope Boundary\n\nThis change protects against accidental or confused local tool behavior after sandbox startup.\nIt does not claim containment of a malicious vendor executable, a compromised runtime, same-user\nraces, damage inside an authorized writable root, or exfiltration through an allowed destination\nsuch as GitHub. It strips proxy and code-injection environment variables required to preserve the\nSRT boundary, but vendor credentials deliberately supplied to a CLI remain readable by that CLI.\nRequest-time secret substitution is dg-08; broader credential brokering and cloud execution remain\nowned by `add-sandboxed-harness-execution`.\n\ndg-03's factual `posture.filesystem` means a per-session workspace exists; it is not a security\nattestation and never satisfies a router request for `sandbox`. Wrapping a local submission CLI\nalso does not imply that a remote worker is sandboxed.\n\n## Approaches Considered\n\n### Shared SRT local-process backend (selected)\n\nOne policy renderer and one lifecycle-owning runner cover every current local CLI sink. It enforces\nthe already-authored isolation and network decisions without creating a second router.\n\n### Vendor-native flags only\n\nRejected. Vendor flags differ, omit network enforcement, and leave vendors without a native\nsandbox unprotected.\n\n### Coordinator-managed containers\n\nDeferred. A container/control-plane backend belongs to the downstream sandboxed-harness change;\ndg-07 supplies the local backend and renderer seam it consumes.\n\n## Impact\n\n- New shared runtime: `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` and local process backend helpers.\n- Modified execution sinks: review dispatcher and autopilot local-provider dispatch.\n- Modified coordinator: exact-agent policy export and durable sandbox audit endpoint.\n- Modified config projection: effective per-mode isolation reaches standalone adapters.\n- New pinned optional tool dependency: SRT 0.0.77.\n- New contracts, tests, operational documentation, and real-runtime probes.\n- New capable-host GitHub Actions evidence gate, with a recorded configured-vendor CLI pass.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRemoving a mode's `sandbox` decision restores the byte-compatible local process path. Removing or\nbreaking the runtime does not silently claim enforcement: the preflight records a durable degraded\nevent before the legacy command may run.\n"}]},"isError":false}
{"type":"tool_execution_end","toolCallId":"chatcmpl-tool-12d11ec531be4ac8b5649e0f36b3e13a","toolName":"read","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Design: Dispatch sandbox enforcement\n\n## Context\n\ndg-02 supplies structured vendor results, dg-03 supplies factual environment posture, dg-05\npins isolation vocabulary and fallback, and dg-06 carries one immutable routing decision. dg-07\nis the execution consumer. The current two subprocess call families are the multi-vendor review\ndispatcher and autopilot's local Pi provider.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D1 — Consume one immutable execution context\n\n`DispatchExecutionContext` carries the exact agent id, dispatch mode, isolation, decision id,\nprovenance, location, enforcement scope, and canonical root. The roadmap host constructs it at\nthe dispatch boundary from dg-06's validated assignment plus the managed worktree root and passes\nit through `PhaseDispatchPayload.execution_context`. `CliVendorAdapter.dispatch()`,\n`dispatch_async()`, and `poll_for_result()` receive the same explicit context. Standalone panel\ncallers construct one context at their adapter boundary from the exact lane's mode override, then\nentry value, and the invocation cwd validated through `checkout_policy.py`. A router-sourced\ncontext requires a non-null decision id. No renderer or backend calls routing or derives a root\nfrom ambient process cwd.\n\nContext producers are explicit:\n\n| Caller | Assignment fields | Execution root |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Routed roadmap/autopilot phase | Copy decision id, agent, isolation, location, and mode from the persisted dg-06 decision into payload v2 | Host adds the validated managed-worktree root |\n| Standalone vendor panel | Resolve exact-lane mode override, then entry isolation, exactly once | Adapter validates its explicit invocation cwd |\n| Autopilot local provider | Consume payload v2 unchanged; no legacy reconstruction | Required in the embedded context |\n\ndg-03 posture is diagnostic evidence only. Its filesystem bit means a per-session workspace, not\ncredential containment; its network bit does not prove equivalence to the active coordinator\npolicy. Neither bit satisfies `isolation=sandbox`.\n\n### D2 — One local process backend, not one list wrapper\n\nAll vendor CLI execution sites call `skills/shared/local_process_backend.py`. The pure renderer in\n`sandbox_profile.py` returns settings and a digest; an impure prepared-command context manager\nvalidates runtime/root/policy and materializes a unique 0600 file. The backend constructs argv and\nenvironment and owns process-group termination and cleanup. `build_command()` remains pure and\nvendor-specific.\n\nThe argv is `[absolute_srt, \"--settings\", settings_path, \"--\", absolute_vendor, ...]` as\ndocumented by SRT. Options that weaken nested, network, Unix-socket, local-binding, or Apple Event\nisolation are never project-configurable.\n\n### D3 — Mode-aware filesystem policy\n\nReview and validation-shaped commands receive no project write roots. Alternative, quick,\nimplementation, and documentation-shaped commands may write only the strict canonical worktree\nroot. Every sandboxed command receives a backend-owned, per-launch state root used for HOME,\nXDG state/config/cache, and runtime temporary files, so vendor CLIs do not need write access to\nthe operator's home. Read-only credential inputs and required environment credential keys remain\nexplicit per-vendor configuration; no renderer hard-codes them. The root must exist, equal `git\nrev-parse --show-toplevel`, pass the existing `checkout_policy.py` managed-worktree check, and\nmust not be `/`, the user's home, or the shared checkout.\n\nThe worktree `.git` pointer and linked-worktree common Git metadata are explicitly denied for\nwrites. A sandboxed worker may edit files but skill prompts do not ask it to commit; the host\norchestrator validates and creates the save-point commit after collecting the worker result. This\navoids granting one agent write access to shared objects and refs.\nSymlink escapes are rejected/tested; hardlink aliasing is measured and documented as a residual\nsame-user risk rather than overstated as contained.\n\n### D4 — Exact-agent, default-deny network export\n\nThe coordinator exports a snapshot from the exact agent's profile assignment plus global rules.\nThe snapshot uses a closed SRT-compatible hostname plus separately range-checked port grammar,\nexplicit scope and priority, schema revision, and canonical SHA-256 digest. Migration 044 adds\n`updated_at` and an atomic exact-agent export function; `policy_revision` is the maximum included\nrow update timestamp plus row count, while the digest is the canonical content change detector.\nDisabled rules are absent.\n\nSRT's deny-first semantics cannot represent every ordered SQL policy exactly. Rendering therefore\nkeeps every applicable deny and only authored allows; conflicts become narrower. New writes are\nvalidated against the export grammar. Any legacy malformed applicable rule makes the entire export\nunrenderable and therefore deny-all; rules are never silently omitted. An unavailable snapshot\nbecomes deny-all. A default-allow snapshot is not renderable by this backend and fails closed. The\nexport contract is authoritative for sandbox execution; the older advisory SQL matcher is not used\nto construct SRT settings.\n\nProvider endpoints are not hard-coded in the renderer. Current seed policy lacks several vendor\nAPI domains, so dg-07 does not flip existing local lanes to `sandbox`; rollout requires an\nauthored endpoint inventory and a successful preflight. The controlled acceptance CLI exercises\nenforcement independently of production vendor endpoints.\n\nThe autopilot `local` provider is rollout-ineligible under `sandbox` until its authored hostname\nand port are exportable and SRT supports the destination class. Loopback, link-local, private-IP,\nor mDNS rejection is a fail-closed policy/capability outcome, never a fail-open reason.\n\n### D5 — Sanitize boundary-shaping environment, do not claim secret brokering\n\nThe environment passed to SRT itself and inherited by its child removes inherited proxy variables,\nloader/startup injection variables, Git path/config overrides, and untrusted temp settings that\ncan alter SRT or its child. This prevents an ambient parent proxy from bypassing SRT address\nchecks. The unsandboxed compatibility path retains the caller's original environment byte for\nbyte. Runtime discovery records absolute Node, SRT entrypoint, `bwrap`, `socat`, and `rg` paths and\nconstructs a minimal trusted PATH from their parent directories; vendor executables are absolute\nand inherited descriptors are closed. Remaining required vendor\ncredentials are still readable by the vendor process; dg-08 owns request-time substitution and\nthe downstream sandboxed-harness change owns broader credential brokering.\n\n### D6 — Narrow fail-open with durable evidence\n\nOnly unsupported OS, missing/incompatible pinned runtime, or failed pre-launch capability probe\nmay run the original command. The backend first writes a durable coordinator event; if unavailable,\nit appends and fsyncs JSONL under\n`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/agentic-coding-tools/sandbox-events/outbox.jsonl`, with a 0700\nparent, 0600 file, advisory lock, and directory fsync. The path is outside every checkout and is\nnever exposed as sandbox-writable. Failure of both blocks dispatch. Unsafe root,\nunrenderable policy, materialization failure, and all post-SRT-start failures fail closed.\n\nEach later event attempt drains older outbox entries before writing the new one, removing a record\nonly after the endpoint acknowledges its `event_id`. Migration 044 makes `event_id` unique; replay\nreturns the original durable audit row id. Audit payloads\ncontain key names and digests, never prompt/argv bodies, settings bodies, or secret values.\n\n### D7 — Pin and probe SRT\n\nThe repository pins `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 with lockfile integrity and Node\n>=20.11.0. `install.sh` and CI may run `npm ci` in `tools/sandbox-runtime`; dispatch performs no\ninstallation. Discovery order is an explicit absolute override, then the dispatcher's own Git\ntop-level `tools/sandbox-runtime` installation, then unavailable. Runtime copies never resolve\nrelative to `__file__`. The backend launches the absolute Node binary and pinned absolute SRT JS\nentrypoint only after package version and lockfile integrity metadata match. Versions before\n0.0.16 are forbidden by the official network-escape advisory.\n\nLinux preflight checks `bwrap`, `socat`, `rg`, supported architecture/seccomp conditions,\nuser-namespace/AppArmor viability, and a no-op sandbox launch. macOS checks the supported native\nbackend and a no-op launch. An unsandboxed fallback is\nallowed only after either the coordinator event or the durable outbox record succeeds.\n\n### Pure renderer and lifecycle-owning backend\n\n`skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` provides:\n\n- pure, deterministic SRT settings rendering;\n- mode-aware filesystem policy (`review` has no project write roots; write-capable modes are\n  confined to the canonical worktree root; every lane gets an ephemeral vendor-state root);\n- a prepared-command lifecycle that owns a unique mode-0600 settings file, sanitized environment,\n  runtime identity, policy digest, process group, and cleanup;\n- an additive renderer seam for future runtimes.\n\nThe reviewed runtime is `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 on Node >=20.11.0. The repository\npins the package and integrity and never installs it during dispatch. Setup/CI install the pin;\nruntime discovery is explicit absolute override, then the dispatcher's Git-root installation,\nthen unavailable. The runtime is accepted only when package metadata and integrity match. On Linux\nthe preflight also verifies `bubblewrap`, `socat`,\n`ripgrep`, user-namespace capability, architecture/seccomp support, and a real no-op SRT launch.\n\nOfficial runtime sources:\n\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/README.md\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/package.json\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-9gqj-5w7c-vx47\n\n### One local command backend\n\nThe shared backend replaces direct vendor subprocess launches in `CliVendorAdapter` sync submit,\nasync submit and poll paths, and in `autopilot/scripts/provider_dispatch.py`. Poll enforcement\nfailures are collection failures retried to the existing deadline, not terminal remote-task\nfailures. A structural guard\nprevents future vendor CLI subprocess sinks outside the backend. Non-sandbox decisions preserve\nargv, stdin, cwd, timeout, and result behavior.\n\n### Loud, bounded degradation\n\nFail-open is restricted to facts known before a vendor process starts: unsupported OS, missing or\nincompatible pinned runtime, or failed platform capability preflight. Those cases warn, durably\naudit `applied=false`, and run the original command. Unsafe roots, malformed policy, settings\nmaterialization errors, and audit/outbox failures fail closed. Once SRT starts, a timeout or\nunknown failure never triggers an unsandboxed retry because doing so could execute work twice.\n\n## Scope Boundary\n\nThis change protects against accidental or confused local tool behavior after sandbox startup.\nIt does not claim containment of a malicious vendor executable, a compromised runtime, same-user\nraces, damage inside an authorized writable root, or exfiltration through an allowed destination\nsuch as GitHub. It strips proxy and code-injection environment variables required to preserve the\nSRT boundary, but vendor credentials deliberately supplied to a CLI remain readable by that CLI.\nRequest-time secret substitution is dg-08; broader credential brokering and cloud execution remain\nowned by `add-sandboxed-harness-execution`.\n\ndg-03's factual `posture.filesystem` means a per-session workspace exists; it is not a security\nattestation and never satisfies a router request for `sandbox`. Wrapping a local submission CLI\nalso does not imply that a remote worker is sandboxed.\n\n## Approaches Considered\n\n### Shared SRT local-process backend (selected)\n\nOne policy renderer and one lifecycle-owning runner cover every current local CLI sink. It enforces\nthe already-authored isolation and network decisions without creating a second router.\n\n### Vendor-native flags only\n\nRejected. Vendor flags differ, omit network enforcement, and leave vendors without a native\nsandbox unprotected.\n\n### Coordinator-managed containers\n\nDeferred. A container/control-plane backend belongs to the downstream sandboxed-harness change;\ndg-07 supplies the local backend and renderer seam it consumes.\n\n## Impact\n\n- New shared runtime: `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` and local process backend helpers.\n- Modified execution sinks: review dispatcher and autopilot local-provider dispatch.\n- Modified coordinator: exact-agent policy export and durable sandbox audit endpoint.\n- Modified config projection: effective per-mode isolation reaches standalone adapters.\n- New pinned optional tool dependency: SRT 0.0.77.\n- New contracts, tests, operational documentation, and real-runtime probes.\n- New capable-host GitHub Actions evidence gate, with a recorded configured-vendor CLI pass.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRemoving a mode's `sandbox` decision restores the byte-compatible local process path. Removing or\nbreaking the runtime does not silently claim enforcement: the preflight records a durable degraded\nevent before the legacy command may run.\n"}],"isError":false,"timestamp":1790211076423}}

Read-only credential inputs and required environment credential keys remain\nexplicit per-vendor configuration; no renderer hard-codes them. Any legacy malformed applicable rule makes the entire export\nunrenderable and therefore deny-all; rules are never silently omitted. An unavailable snapshot\nbecomes deny-all. The current two subprocess call families are the multi-vendor review\ndispatcher and autopilot's local Pi provider.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D1 — Consume one immutable execution context\n\n`DispatchExecutionContext` carries the exact agent id, dispatch mode, isolation, decision id,\nprovenance, location, enforcement scope, and canonical root. The roadmap host constructs it at\nthe dispatch boundary from dg-06's validated assignment plus the managed worktree root and passes\nit through `PhaseDispatchPayload.execution_context`. `CliVendorAdapter.dispatch()`,\n`dispatch_async()`, and `poll_for_result()` receive the same explicit context. Standalone panel\ncallers construct one context at their adapter boundary from the exact lane's mode override, then\nentry value, and the invocation cwd validated through `checkout_policy.py`. A router-sourced\ncontext requires a non-null decision id. No renderer or backend calls routing or derives a root\nfrom ambient process cwd.\n\nContext producers are explicit:\n\n| Caller | Assignment fields | Execution root |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Routed roadmap/autopilot phase | Copy decision id, agent, isolation, location, and mode from the persisted dg-06 decision into payload v2 | Host adds the validated managed-worktree root |\n| Standalone vendor panel | Resolve exact-lane mode override, then entry isolation, exactly once | Adapter validates its explicit invocation cwd |\n| Autopilot local provider | Consume payload v2 unchanged; no legacy reconstruction | Required in the embedded context |\n\ndg-03 posture is diagnostic evidence only. Its filesystem bit means a per-session workspace, not\ncredential containment; its network bit does not prove equivalence to the active coordinator\npolicy. Neither bit satisfies `isolation=sandbox`.\n\n### D2 — One local process backend, not one list wrapper\n\nAll vendor CLI execution sites call `skills/shared/local_process_backend.py`. The pure renderer in\n`sandbox_profile.py` returns settings and a digest; an impure prepared-command context manager\nvalidates runtime/root/policy and materializes a unique 0600 file. The backend constructs argv and\nenvironment and owns process-group termination and cleanup. `build_command()` remains pure and\nvendor-specific.\n\nThe argv is `[absolute_srt, \"--settings\", settings_path, \"--\", absolute_vendor, ...]` as\ndocumented by SRT. Options that weaken nested, network, Unix-socket, local-binding, or Apple Event\nisolation are never project-configurable.\n\n### D3 — Mode-aware filesystem policy\n\nReview and validation-shaped commands receive no project write roots. Alternative, quick,\nimplementation, and documentation-shaped commands may write only the strict canonical worktree\nroot. Every sandboxed command receives a backend-owned, per-launch state root used for HOME,\nXDG state/config/cache, and runtime temporary files, so vendor CLIs do not need write access to\nthe operator's home. Read-only credential inputs and required environment credential keys remain\nexplicit per-vendor configuration; no renderer hard-codes them. The root must exist, equal `git\nrev-parse --show-toplevel`, pass the existing `checkout_policy.py` managed-worktree check, and\nmust not be `/`, the user's home, or the shared checkout.\n\nThe worktree `.git` pointer and linked-worktree common Git metadata are explicitly denied for\nwrites. A sandboxed worker may edit files but skill prompts do not ask it to commit; the host\norchestrator validates and creates the save-point commit after collecting the worker result. This\navoids granting one agent write access to shared objects and refs.\nSymlink escapes are rejected/tested; hardlink aliasing is measured and documented as a residual\nsame-user risk rather than overstated as contained.\n\n### D4 — Exact-agent, default-deny network export\n\nThe coordinator exports a snapshot from the exact agent's profile assignment plus global rules.\nThe snapshot uses a closed SRT-compatible hostname plus separately range-checked port grammar,\nexplicit scope and priority, schema revision, and canonical SHA-256 digest. Migration 044 adds\n`updated_at` and an atomic exact-agent export function; `policy_revision` is the maximum included\nrow update timestamp plus row count, while the digest is the canonical content change detector.\nDisabled rules are absent.\n\nSRT's deny-first semantics cannot represent every ordered SQL policy exactly. Rendering therefore\nkeeps every applicable deny and only authored allows; conflicts become narrower. New writes are\nvalidated against the export grammar. Any legacy malformed applicable rule makes the entire export\nunrenderable and therefore deny-all; rules are never silently omitted. An unavailable snapshot\nbecomes deny-all. A default-allow snapshot is not renderable by this backend and fails closed. The\nexport contract is authoritative for sandbox execution; the older advisory SQL matcher is not used\nto construct SRT settings.\n\nProvider endpoints are not hard-coded in the renderer. Current seed policy lacks several vendor\nAPI domains, so dg-07 does not flip existing local lanes to `sandbox`; rollout requires an\nauthored endpoint inventory and a successful preflight. The controlled acceptance CLI exercises\nenforcement independently of production vendor endpoints.\n\nThe autopilot `local` provider is rollout-ineligible under `sandbox` until its authored hostname\nand port are exportable and SRT supports the destination class. Loopback, link-local, private-IP,\nor mDNS rejection is a fail-closed policy/capability outcome, never a fail-open reason.\n\n### D5 — Sanitize boundary-shaping environment, do not claim secret brokering\n\nThe environment passed to SRT itself and inherited by its child removes inherited proxy variables,\nloader/startup injection variables, Git path/config overrides, and untrusted temp settings that\ncan alter SRT or its child. This prevents an ambient parent proxy from bypassing SRT address\nchecks. The unsandboxed compatibility path retains the caller's original environment byte for\nbyte. Runtime discovery records absolute Node, SRT entrypoint, `bwrap`, `socat`, and `rg` paths and\nconstructs a minimal trusted PATH from their parent directories; vendor executables are absolute\nand inherited descriptors are closed. Remaining required vendor\ncredentials are still readable by the vendor process; dg-08 owns request-time substitution and\nthe downstream sandboxed-harness change owns broader credential brokering.\n\n### D6 — Narrow fail-open with durable evidence\n\nOnly unsupported OS, missing/incompatible pinned runtime, or failed pre-launch capability probe\nmay run the original command. The backend first writes a durable coordinator event; if unavailable,\nit appends and fsyncs JSONL under\n`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/agentic-coding-tools/sandbox-events/outbox.jsonl`, with a 0700\nparent, 0600 file, advisory lock, and directory fsync. The path is outside every checkout and is\nnever exposed as sandbox-writable. Failure of both blocks dispatch. Unsafe root,\nunrenderable policy, materialization failure, and all post-SRT-start failures fail closed.\n\nEach later event attempt drains older outbox entries before writing the new one, removing a record\nonly after the endpoint acknowledges its `event_id`. Migration 044 makes `event_id` unique; replay\nreturns the original durable audit row id. Audit payloads\ncontain key names and digests, never prompt/argv bodies, settings bodies, or secret values.\n\n### D7 — Pin and probe SRT\n\nThe repository pins `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 with lockfile integrity and Node\n>=20.11.0. `install.sh` and CI may run `npm ci` in `tools/sandbox-runtime`; dispatch performs no\ninstallation. Discovery order is an explicit absolute override, then the dispatcher's own Git\ntop-level `tools/sandbox-runtime` installation, then unavailable. There is no cancellation subprocess\ntoday; any future configured cancellation command is covered by the same structural guard. The\nactual invocation cwd is the policy root. A pre-launch enforcement denial during polling is a\nretryable collection condition until the existing poll deadline; it must not close a still-running\nremote task as a vendor failure. On timeout the backend starts a new session, sends TERM to the\nprocess group, waits a bounded grace period, sends KILL if required, waits, and then cleans owned\nmaterial. No cancellation subprocess exists today; any future configured vendor cancellation\ncommand SHALL use the same backend.\n\n#### Scenario: Every vendor lifecycle command uses the backend\n\nWHEN a configured local vendor CLI is submitted, polled, or run synchronously\nTHEN exactly one shared backend invocation SHALL own process creation\nAND a structural guard SHALL reject new direct vendor subprocess sinks.\n\n#### Scenario: Non-sandbox behavior remains compatible\n\nWHEN effective isolation is `none` or `worktree`\nTHEN the backend SHALL preserve argv, stdin, cwd, timeout, and result behavior\nAND no sandbox settings file SHALL be created.\n\n### Requirement: Enforcement SHALL consume the immutable routing decision\n\nThe backend SHALL consume the dg-06 routing decision attached to dispatch context and SHALL NOT\ncall routing again. A standalone caller without routed context SHALL resolve dg-05's exact-lane\nfallback once at the adapter boundary and record that provenance.\n\n#### Scenario: Routed execution is not re-resolved\n\nWHEN dispatch context carries a validated routing decision and isolation assignment\nTHEN the same decision identifier and assignment SHALL appear in the execution audit\nAND no router request SHALL occur during rendering, preparation, or process execution.\n\n#### Scenario: Standalone dispatch resolves the exact lane\n\nWHEN a review-panel dispatch has no routed context\nTHEN effective isolation SHALL be resolved from its exact agent id and dispatch mode\nAND an entry-level value SHALL be inherited only when that mode has no override.\n\n### Requirement: Sandbox rendering SHALL be pure and mode-aware\n\nThe SRT renderer SHALL be deterministic and side-effect free. Review mode SHALL receive no project\nworktree write access. Write-capable modes MAY write only beneath a strictly resolved canonical Git\nworktree root. Per-launch vendor state SHALL be isolated from the operator's home. Reads of named\ncredential locations SHALL be denied except for explicit per-vendor credential inputs pending\ndg-08.\n\n#### Scenario: Review is read-only\n\nWHEN a `sandbox` decision is rendered for documented internal paths MAY remain\nwritable.\n\n#### Scenario: Write-capable work is root-confined\n\nWHEN a `sandbox` decision is rendered for an alternative or quick dispatch\nTHEN the only project write root SHALL be the canonical worktree root\nAND the worktree `.git` pointer and common Git metadata SHALL be denied for writes\nAND writes through path or symlink escapes SHALL fail.\n\n#### Scenario: Rendering has no effects\n\nWHEN identical validated context and policy inputs are rendered twice\nTHEN the policy documents and digests SHALL be identical\nAND rendering SHALL NOT write files, spawn processes, or contact a service.\n\n### Requirement: Prepared sandbox commands SHALL own lifecycle and truthful state\n\nThe impure preparation layer SHALL own a unique runtime, or failed platform capability probe. A warning and durable audit or\noutbox event SHALL exist before launch. Unsafe roots, malformed policies, and audit persistence\nfailure SHALL fail closed. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Loading + validation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _default_agents_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \"agents.yaml\"\n\n\ndef _default_secrets_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \".secrets.yaml\"\n\n\ndef load_agents_config(\n    path: Path | None = None,\n    *,\n    secrets_path: Path | None = None,\n) -> list[AgentEntry]:\n    \"\"\"Load and validate ``agents.yaml``.\n\n    Args:\n        path: Path to agents YAML file.\n        secrets_path: Path to ``.secrets.yaml`` for ``${VAR}`` interpolation\n            in ``api_key`` fields.\n\n    Returns:\n        List of validated :class:`AgentEntry` objects.\n\n    Raises:\n        FileNotFoundError: If *path* does not exist.\n        jsonschema.ValidationError: If the data fails schema validation.\n        ValueError: On duplicate agent names or duplicate ``profile`` values.\n    \"\"\"\n    if path is None:\n        path = _default_agents_path()\n    if secrets_path is None:\n        secrets_path = _default_secrets_path()\n\n    with open(path) as fh:\n        raw = yaml.safe_load(fh)\n\n    if raw is None:\n        raise ValueError(\"Empty agents.yaml file\")\n\n    validate(instance=raw, schema=AGENTS_SCHEMA)\n\n    secrets = _load_secrets_file(secrets_path)\n    entries: list[AgentEntry] = []\n    seen_names: set[str] = set()\n    #: profile name -> the agent that claimed it, so the second claimant can be\n    #: named in the error.\n    seen_profiles: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    for name, agent_data in raw[\"agents\"].items():\n        if name in seen_names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name in file order, so the last entry silently\n        # overwrites the first one's trust level and operations. An agent could\n        # then be promoted to admin without its own trust_level line changing,\n        # and neither orphan disabling nor the registry invariant check would\n        # notice. One agent, one profile row.\n        profile_name = agent_data[\"profile\"]\n        if profile_name in seen_profiles:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"Duplicate profile: '{profile_name}' is declared by both \"\n                f\"'{seen_profiles[profile_name]}' and '{name}'. Each agent needs \"\n                f\"its own profile, or the later entry silently overwrites the \"\n                f\"earlier one's trust level and operations.\"\n            )\n ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name seen_profiles[profile_name] = name\n\n        raw_key = agent_data.get(\"api_key\")\n        resolved_key: str | None = None\n        if raw_key:\n            resolved_key = interpolate(raw_key, ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Loading + validation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _default_agents_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \"agents.yaml\"\n\n\ndef _default_secrets_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \".secrets.yaml\"\n\n\ndef load_agents_config(\n    path: Path | None = None,\n    *,\n    secrets_path: Path | None = None,\n) -> list[AgentEntry]:\n    \"\"\"Load and validate ``agents.yaml``.\n\n    Args:\n        path: Path to agents YAML file.\n        secrets_path: Path to ``.secrets.yaml`` for ``${VAR}`` interpolation\n            in ``api_key`` fields.\n\n    Returns:\n        List of validated :class:`AgentEntry` objects.\n\n    Raises:\n        FileNotFoundError: If *path* does not exist.\n        jsonschema.ValidationError: If the data fails schema validation.\n        ValueError: On duplicate agent names or duplicate ``profile`` values.\n    \"\"\"\n    if path is None:\n        path = _default_agents_path()\n    if secrets_path is None:\n        secrets_path = _default_secrets_path()\n\n    with open(path) as fh:\n        raw = yaml.safe_load(fh)\n\n    if raw is None:\n        raise ValueError(\"Empty agents.yaml file\")\n\n    validate(instance=raw, schema=AGENTS_SCHEMA)\n\n    secrets = _load_secrets_file(secrets_path)\n    entries: list[AgentEntry] = []\n    seen_names: set[str] = set()\n    #: profile name -> the agent that claimed it, so the second claimant can be\n    #: named in the error.\n    seen_profiles: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    for name, agent_data in raw[\"agents\"].items():\n        if name in seen_names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name in file order, so the last entry silently\n        # overwrites the first one's trust level and operations. An agent could\n        # then be promoted to admin without its own trust_level line changing,\n        # and neither orphan disabling nor the registry invariant check would\n        # notice. One agent, one profile row.\n        profile_name = agent_data[\"profile\"]\n        if profile_name in seen_profiles:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"Duplicate profile: '{profile_name}' is declared by both \"\n                f\"'{seen_profiles[profile_name]}' and '{name}'. Each agent needs \"\n                f\"its own profile, or the later entry silently overwrites the \"\n                f\"earlier one's trust level and operations.\"\n            )\n        seen_profiles[profile_name] = name\n\n        raw_key = agent_data.get(\"api_key\")\n        resolved_key: str | None = None\n        if raw_key:\n            resolved_key = interpolate(raw_key, secrets)\n            # Keep unresolved ${VAR} placeholders so that\n            # _resolve_api_key_from_openbao() can extract the variable\n            # name and fetch the secret from OpenBao at runtime.\n\n        cli_config: CliConfig | None = None\n        raw_cli = agent_data.get(\"cli\")\n        if raw_cli:\n            def _parse_mode(mode_data: dict[str, Any]) -> ModeConfig:\n                poll_config: PollConfig | None = None\n                raw_poll = mode_data.get(\"poll\")\n                if raw_poll:\n                    poll_config = PollConfig(\n                        command_template=raw_poll[\"command_template\"],\n                        result_protocol=raw_poll[\"result_protocol\"],\n                        interval_seconds=raw_poll.get(\n                            \"interval_seconds\", 30,\n                        ),\n                        timeout_seconds=raw_poll.get(\n                            \"timeout_seconds\", 600,\n                        ),\n                    )\n                return ModeConfig(\n                    args=mode_data[\"args\"],\n                    async_dispatch=mode_data.get(\"async\", False),\n                    isolation=mode_data.get(\"isolation\"),\n                    poll=poll_config,\n                )\n\n            cli_config = CliConfig(\n                command=raw_cli[\"command\"],\n model_flag=raw_cli[\"model_flag\"],\n                model=raw_cli.get(\"model\"),\n                model_fallbacks=raw_cli.get(\"model_fallbacks\", []),\n ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# API key identity generation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n        logger.warning(\n            \"Failed to resolve API key from OpenBao for agent '%s' — \"\n            \"falling back to static resolution\",\n            agent.name,\n            exc_info=True,\n        )\n        return agent.api_key\n\n\nclass DuplicateApiKeyError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Two registry agents resolve to the same API key (design D6).\n\n    A shared key is an identity-confusion bug: the coordinator would attribute\n    both principals' operations to whichever agent happened to win the map, so\n    the audit trail silently lies. Fail at load with both agent names instead.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, first_agent: str, second_agent: str) -> None:\n        self.first_agent = first_agent\n        self.second_agent = second_agent\n        super().__init__(\n            f\"Duplicate resolved API key: agents '{first_agent}' and \"\n            f\"'{second_agent}' resolve to the same value. Every agent needs \"\n            f\"its own key — a shared key makes audit attribution ambiguous.\"\n        )\n\n\ndef get_api_key_identities(\n    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Generate ``COORDINATION_API_KEY_IDENTITIES`` for the full agent roster.\n\n    Every agent with a resolvable ``api_key`` receives an identity entry,\n    regardless of declared ``transport`` (design D5): the MCP server's\n    HTTP-proxy fallback makes local agents HTTP principals in practice, so\n    ``transport`` is dispatch metadata only and does not gate identity.\n\n    When OpenBao is enabled, attempts to resolve API keys from OpenBao\n    for agents with ``openbao_role_id``. Falls back to static interpolation.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dict mapping resolved API key values to\n        ``{\"agent_id\": ..., \"agent_type\": ...}``.\n\n    Raises:\n        DuplicateApiKeyError: If two agents resolve to the same key.\n    \"\"\"\n    if agents is None:\n        agents = load_agents_config()\n\n    # Check if OpenBao is available for key resolution\n    openbao_enabled = bool(os.environ.get(\"BAO_ADDR\"))\n\n    identities: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}\n    for agent in agents:\n        key = agent.api_key\n        if openbao_enabled and agent.openbao_role_id:\n            resolved = _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent)\n            if resolved:\n                key = resolved\n\n        if not key:\n            continue\n\n        # Skip unresolved ${VAR} placeholders — they're not usable as\n        # identity keys unless resolved via OpenBao above.\n        if _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(key):\n            continue\n\n        if key in identities:\n            raise DuplicateApiKeyError(identities[key][\"agent_id\"], agent.name)\n        identities[key] = {\n            \"agent_id\": agent.name,\n            \"agent_type\": agent.type,\n        }\n    return identities\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Registry → agent_profiles projection (design D1 / D2)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: Operations every projected profile receives. Migration 007 granted\n#: ``get_my_profile`` to every seeded profile without exception: reading one's\n#: own profile is not a privilege, it is how an agent discovers its own limits.\nUNIVERSAL_OPERATIONS: tuple[str, ...] = (\"get_my_profile\",)\n\n#: ``agents.yaml`` capability → the coordination operations it authorizes.\n#: Derived from the operation lists the hand-written seeds granted (migrations\n#: 007 / 019 / 022 / 026); ``tests/test_profile_sync.py`` pins the mapping\n#: against the grants ``claude_code_local`` carries today.\nCAPABILITY_OPERATIONS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {\n    \"lock\": (\"acquire_lock\", \"release_lock\", \"check_locks\"),\n    \"queue\": (\"get_work\", \"get_task\", \"complete_work\", \"submit_work\"),\n    \"memory\": (\"remember\", \"recall\"),\n    \"guardrails\": (\"check_guardrails\",),\n    \"handoff\": (\"write_handoff\", \"read_handoff\"),\n    \"discover\": (\"register_session\", \"discover_agents\", \"heartbeat\"),\n    \"audit\": (\"query_audit\",),\n    \"feature_registry\": (\"register_feature\", \"deregister_feature\"),\n    \"vendor_limit_reporter\": (\"report_vendor_rate_limit\",),\n}\n\n#: Operations granted by *trust level* rather than by capability, as\n#: ``(minimum trust level, operations)`` pairs. Migration 022 granted the merge\n#: queue operations with ``WHERE trust_level >= 3`` — no capability in\n#: ``agents.yaml`` covers them, so the projection needs this second dimension\n#: to reproduce the grants the migrations made.\nTRUST_DERIVED_OPERATIONS: tuple[tuple[int, tuple[str, ...]], ...] = (\n    (\n        int(TrustLevel.ELEVATED),\n        (\n            \"register_feature\",\n            \"deregister_feature\",\n            \"enqueue_merge\",\n            \"run_pre_merge_checks\",\n            \"mark_merged\",\n            \"remove_from_merge_queue\",\n            \"publish_work_projection\",\n            \"report_vendor_rate_limit\",\n        ),\n    ),\n)\n\n#: Profile rows the registry deliberately does NOT own (design D2 amendment).\n#:\n#: ``agents.yaml`` describes *harness identities*: things that can be\n#: dispatched, that speak a transport, and that authenticate. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# API key identity generation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n        logger.warning(\n            \"Failed to resolve API key from OpenBao for agent '%s' — \"\n            \"falling back to static resolution\",\n            agent.name,\n            exc_info=True,\n        )\n        return agent.api_key\n\n\nclass DuplicateApiKeyError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Two registry agents resolve to the same API key (design D6).\n\n    A shared key is an identity-confusion bug: the coordinator would attribute\n    both principals' operations to whichever agent happened to win the map, so\n    the audit trail silently lies. Fail at load with both agent names instead.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, first_agent: str, second_agent: str) -> None:\n        self.first_agent = first_agent\n        self.second_agent = second_agent\n        super().__init__(\n            f\"Duplicate resolved API key: agents '{first_agent}' and \"\n            f\"'{second_agent}' resolve to the same value. Every agent needs \"\n            f\"its own key — a shared key makes audit attribution ambiguous.\"\n        )\n\n\ndef get_api_key_identities(\n    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Generate ``COORDINATION_API_KEY_IDENTITIES`` for the full agent roster.\n\n    Every agent with a resolvable ``api_key`` receives an identity entry,\n    regardless of declared ``transport`` (design D5): the MCP server's\n    HTTP-proxy fallback makes local agents HTTP principals in practice, so\n    ``transport`` is dispatch metadata only and does not gate identity.\n\n    When OpenBao is enabled, attempts to resolve API keys from OpenBao\n    for agents with ``openbao_role_id``. Falls back to static interpolation.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dict mapping resolved API key values to\n        ``{\"agent_id\": ..., \"agent_type\": ...}``.\n\n    Raises:\n        DuplicateApiKeyError: If two agents resolve to the same key.\n    \"\"\"\n    if agents is None:\n        agents = load_agents_config()\n\n    # Check if OpenBao is available for key resolution\n    openbao_enabled = bool(os.environ.get(\"BAO_ADDR\"))\n\n    identities: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}\n    for agent in agents:\n        key = agent.api_key\n        if openbao_enabled and agent.openbao_role_id:\n            resolved = _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent)\n            if resolved:\n                key = resolved\n\n        if not key:\n            continue\n\n        # Skip unresolved ${VAR} placeholders — they're not usable as\n        # identity keys unless resolved via OpenBao above.\n        if _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(key):\n            continue\n\n        if key in identities:\n            raise DuplicateApiKeyError(identities[key][\"agent_id\"], agent.name)\n        identities[key] = {\n            \"agent_id\": agent.name,\n            \"agent_type\": agent.type,\n        }\n    return identities\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Registry → agent_profiles projection (design D1 / D2)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: Operations every projected profile receives. ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name seen_profiles[profile_name] = name\n\n        raw_key = agent_data.get(\"api_key\")\n        resolved_key: str | None = None\n        if raw_key:\n            resolved_key = interpolate(raw_key, ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Loading + validation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _default_agents_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \"agents.yaml\"\n\n\ndef _default_secrets_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \".secrets.yaml\"\n\n\ndef load_agents_config(\n    path: Path | None = None,\n    *,\n    secrets_path: Path | None = None,\n) -> list[AgentEntry]:\n    \"\"\"Load and validate ``agents.yaml``.\n\n    Args:\n        path: Path to agents YAML file.\n        secrets_path: Path to ``.secrets.yaml`` for ``${VAR}`` interpolation\n            in ``api_key`` fields.\n\n    Returns:\n        List of validated :class:`AgentEntry` objects.\n\n    Raises:\n        FileNotFoundError: If *path* does not exist.\n        jsonschema.ValidationError: If the data fails schema validation.\n        ValueError: On duplicate agent names or duplicate ``profile`` values.\n    \"\"\"\n    if path is None:\n        path = _default_agents_path()\n    if secrets_path is None:\n        secrets_path = _default_secrets_path()\n\n    with open(path) as fh:\n        raw = yaml.safe_load(fh)\n\n    if raw is None:\n        raise ValueError(\"Empty agents.yaml file\")\n\n    validate(instance=raw, schema=AGENTS_SCHEMA)\n\n    secrets = _load_secrets_file(secrets_path)\n    entries: list[AgentEntry] = []\n    seen_names: set[str] = set()\n    #: profile name -> the agent that claimed it, so the second claimant can be\n    #: named in the error.\n    seen_profiles: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    for name, agent_data in raw[\"agents\"].items():\n        if name in seen_names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name in file order, so the last entry silently\n        # overwrites the first one's trust level and operations. An agent could\n        # then be promoted to admin without its own trust_level line changing,\n        # and neither orphan disabling nor the registry invariant check would\n        # notice. One agent, one profile row.\n        profile_name = agent_data[\"profile\"]\n        if profile_name in seen_profiles:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"Duplicate profile: '{profile_name}' is declared by both \"\n                f\"'{seen_profiles[profile_name]}' and '{name}'. Each agent needs \"\n                f\"its own profile, or the later entry silently overwrites the \"\n                f\"earlier one's trust level and operations.\"\n            )\n        seen_profiles[profile_name] = name\n\n        raw_key = agent_data.get(\"api_key\")\n        resolved_key: str | None = None\n        if raw_key:\n            resolved_key = interpolate(raw_key, secrets)\n            # Keep unresolved ${VAR} placeholders so that\n            # _resolve_api_key_from_openbao() can extract the variable\n            # name and fetch the secret from OpenBao at runtime.\n\n        cli_config: CliConfig | None = None\n        raw_cli = agent_data.get(\"cli\")\n        if raw_cli:\n            def _parse_mode(mode_data: dict[str, Any]) -> ModeConfig:\n                poll_config: PollConfig | None = None\n                raw_poll = mode_data.get(\"poll\")\n                if raw_poll:\n                    poll_config = PollConfig(\n                        command_template=raw_poll[\"command_template\"],\n                        result_protocol=raw_poll[\"result_protocol\"],\n                        interval_seconds=raw_poll.get(\n                            \"interval_seconds\", 30,\n                        ),\n                        timeout_seconds=raw_poll.get(\n                            \"timeout_seconds\", 600,\n                        ),\n                    )\n                return ModeConfig(\n                    args=mode_data[\"args\"],\n                    async_dispatch=mode_data.get(\"async\", False),\n                    isolation=mode_data.get(\"isolation\"),\n                    poll=poll_config,\n                )\n\n            cli_config = CliConfig(\n                command=raw_cli[\"command\"],\n model_flag=raw_cli[\"model_flag\"],\n                model=raw_cli.get(\"model\"),\n                model_fallbacks=raw_cli.get(\"model_fallbacks\", []),\n                prompt_via_stdin=raw_cli.get(\"prompt_via_stdin\", False),\n                prompt_via_flag=raw_cli.get(\"prompt_via_flag\", \"\"),\n                api_key_env=raw_cli.get(\"api_key_env\", \"\"),\n            )\n\n        sdk_config: SdkConfig | None = None\n        raw_sdk = agent_data.get(\"sdk\")\n        if raw_sdk:\n            sdk_config = SdkConfig(\n                package=raw_sdk[\"package\"],\n                model=raw_sdk[\"model\"],\n                method=raw_sdk.get(\"method\", \"messages.create\"),\n                model_fallbacks=raw_sdk.get(\"model_fallbacks\", []),\n                api_key_env=raw_sdk.get(\"api_key_env\", \"\"),\n                max_tokens=raw_sdk.get(\"max_tokens\", 16384),\n api_key=resolved_key,\n                openbao_role_id=agent_data.get(\"openbao_role_id\"),\n                endpoint_kind=agent_data.get(\"endpoint_kind\"),\n ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# API key identity generation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n        logger.warning(\n            \"Failed to resolve API key from OpenBao for agent '%s' — \"\n            \"falling back to static resolution\",\n            agent.name,\n            exc_info=True,\n        )\n        return agent.api_key\n\n\nclass DuplicateApiKeyError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Two registry agents resolve to the same API key (design D6).\n\n    A shared key is an identity-confusion bug: the coordinator would attribute\n    both principals' operations to whichever agent happened to win the map, so\n    the audit trail silently lies. @classmethod\n    def _find_coordinator_dir(cls) -> tuple[str, Path] | None:\n        \"\"\"Discover the agent-coordinator directory from MCP config.\n\n        Reads ``~/.claude.json`` to find the Only consider local agents (transport=mcp) for CLI dispatch\n            if adapter.transport == \"mcp\" and adapter.vendor not in cli_by_vendor:\n                cli_by_vendor[adapter.vendor] = (agent_id, adapter)\n\n        # Collect all SDK adapters\n        sdk_by_vendor: dict[str, tuple[str, SdkVendorAdapter]] = {}\n        for agent_id, adapter in self.sdk_adapters.items():\n            if exclude_vendor and adapter.vendor == exclude_vendor:\n                continue\n            if adapter.vendor not in sdk_by_vendor:\n                sdk_by_vendor[adapter.vendor] = (agent_id, adapter)\n\n        openai_by_vendor: dict[str, tuple[str, Any]] = {}\n        for agent_id, adapter in self.openai_adapters.items():\n            if exclude_vendor and adapter.vendor == exclude_vendor:\n                continue\n            if adapter.vendor not in openai_by_vendor:\n                openai_by_vendor[adapter.vendor] = (agent_id, adapter)\n\n        all_vendors = (\n            set(cli_by_vendor.keys())\n            | set(sdk_by_vendor.keys())\n            | set(openai_by_vendor.keys())\n        )\n        reviewers: list[ReviewerInfo] = []\n\n        for vendor in sorted(all_vendors):\n            # Passed by-value to\n            keep the driver/sub-agent boundary explicit.\n        incoming_handoff: PhaseRecord from the previous phase. Serialized\n            into the prompt so the sub-agent can hydrate it via\n            ``PhaseRecord.from_handoff_payload`` if needed.\n        subagent_runner: Injected callable that actually invokes the\n            harness Agent tool. Transcript is consumed inside this\n        function and never escapes.\n\n    Raises:\n        PhaseEscalationError: After ``max_attempts`` consecutive failures.\n    \"\"\"\n    options = _build_options(phase, state_dict)\n    prompt = _build_prompt(phase, state_dict, incoming_handoff, artifacts_manifest)\n\n    last_error = \"no error captured\"\n    for attempt in range(1, max_attempts + 1):\n        try:\n            result = subagent_runner(prompt=prompt, options=options)\n        except Exception as exc:  # Whitespace around\n    keys/values is tolerated. Per spec D8:\n\n    - Empty input returns ``{}``.\n    - Entries missing ``=`` are warned and skipped.\n    - Unknown phase names (not in :data:`_PHASE_SIGNAL_KEYS`) are warned\n      and skipped — typo protection.\n    - Empty model values are warned and skipped.\n    - Unknown model names pass through (validated downstream by the harness).\n    \"\"\"\n    if not raw or not raw.strip():\n        return {}\n    out: dict[str, str] = {}\n    for entry in raw.split(\",\"):\n        entry = entry.strip()\n        if not entry:\n            continue\n        if \"=\" not in entry:\n            logger.warning(\n                \"%s: malformed entry %r (missing '='); The bridge already\n    # logs a structured warning; no need to double-log here.\n\n    return options\n\n\ndef _build_prompt(\n    phase: str,\n    state_dict: dict[str, Any],\n    incoming_handoff: PhaseRecord,\n    artifacts_manifest: list[str] | None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Assemble the standard sub-agent prompt scaffold.\n\n    Three sections per D6:\n      1. Phase + state context (machine-readable)\n      2. Incoming PhaseRecord JSON (the structured handoff)\n      3. Artifacts manifest (paths the sub-agent should read first)\n    \"\"\"\n    incoming_json = json.dumps(incoming_handoff.to_handoff_payload(), indent=2)\n    state_json = json.dumps(_safe_state_dict(state_dict), indent=2)\n\n    parts = [\n        f\"# Autopilot Phase Sub-Agent — {phase}\",\n        \"\",\n        \"You are running as an autopilot phase sub-agent. The orchestrator — NOT you —\",\n        \"owns every state transition. Editing it directly corrupts the loop.\",\n    ])\n\n\ndef _safe_state_dict(state_dict: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Strip non-serializable values from state_dict so json.dumps succeeds.\"\"\"\n    out: dict[str, Any] = {}\n    for k, v in state_dict.items():\n        try:\n            json.dumps(v)\n        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n            out[k] = repr(v)\n        else:\n            out[k] = v\n    return out\n\n\n# Per spec D6: every non-terminal phase has a _PHASE_TASKS entry. NOT parameterized — every dispatch in this skill uses this exact\n# string and spec scenarios assert it verbatim.\n_PROMPT_SEPARATOR = \"\\n\\n---\\n\\n\"\n\n# OpenSpec change-id pattern (also enforced by OpenSpec itself). The two have to be tracked\n    separately because `os.fdopen` could (theoretically — extremely\n    rare) raise after `mkstemp` returned, in which case the with-block\n    never owns the fd and we'd leak it without an explicit close.\n    \"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    # nosec B108: dir= confines the tempfile to the target directory (not\n    # /tmp), which is the canonical pattern for atomic same-fs replace.\n    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(  # noqa: S108\n        prefix=path.name + \".\",\n        suffix=\".tmp\",\n        dir=str(path.parent),\n    )\n    fd_consumed = False\n    try:\n        fh = os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        fd_consumed = True  # the file object now owns the fd\n        try:\n            json.dump(payload, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)\n            fh.write(\"\\n\")\n        finally:\n            fh.close()\n        os.replace(tmp, path)\n    except Exception:\n        # Two distinct cleanup concerns: an orphaned fd (only when\n        # os.fdopen failed) and an orphaned tmp file (always).\n        if not fd_consumed:\n            try:\n                os.close(fd)\n            except OSError:\n                # Best-effort fd cleanup; the original exception is re-raised\n                # below, so silencing here only suppresses cleanup noise.\n                pass  # nosec B110\n        try:\n            os.unlink(tmp)\n        except OSError:\n            # Best-effort tmp-file cleanup; build_phase_dispatch_payload(\n    phase: str,\n    change_id: str,\n    provider: str | None = None,\n    agent_id: str | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Return a provider-neutral phase str,\n    phase: str,\n    outcome: str,\n    handoff_id: str,\n    *,\n    allow_phase_mismatch: bool = False,\n    change_dir: Path | None = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Update loop-state.json after a phase sub-agent returns (D4).\n\n    ``change_dir`` (roadmap ri-06): on the non-replay path, when *phase* is\n    ``\"GATEKEEPER\"``, also builds and appends a ``\"GATEKEEPER_SHADOW\"``\n    ``phase_history`` entry via ``gatekeeper_shadow.build_shadow_entry`` --\n    the real host-driven GATEKEEPER dispatch protocol\n    (``skills/autopilot/SKILL.md`` Step 1.5: ``build-dispatch`` /\n    ``apply-outcome``) never calls the Python-level ``_phase_gatekeeper``, so\n    this is the only place a production run can record shadow data (Codex\n    review, PR #591, P1). Replay-safe: the shadow judgment is skipped\n    entirely on the replay path above, so a retried ``apply-outcome`` call\n    never doubles the ``decide()`` call count or the shadow record.\n\n    **No-transition contract (design D1 Layer A / Task 3):** this function\n    updates ONLY the fields it owns — ``last_handoff_id``, ``handoff_ids``\n    (append), ``phase_archetype``, and a new ``phase_history`` entry. It\n    NEVER modifies ``current_phase``. The orchestrator is the sole writer\n    of ``current_phase``.\n\n    **Phase-mismatch guard (Task 3.2-3.4):** on the non-replay path, if\n    *phase* does not equal loop-state's ``current_phase`` the call raises\n    ``ValueError`` (surfaced as a non-zero exit by the runner CLI) unless\n    *allow_phase_mismatch* is set. NOT parameterized — every dispatch in this skill uses this exact\n# string and spec scenarios assert it verbatim.\n_PROMPT_SEPARATOR = \"\\n\\n---\\n\\n\"\n\n# OpenSpec change-id pattern (also enforced by OpenSpec itself). The two have to be tracked\n    separately because `os.fdopen` could (theoretically — extremely\n    rare) raise after `mkstemp` returned, in which case the with-block\n    never owns the fd and we'd leak it without an explicit close.\n    \"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    # nosec B108: dir= confines the tempfile to the target directory (not\n    # /tmp), which is the canonical pattern for atomic same-fs replace.\n    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(  # noqa: S108\n        prefix=path.name + \".\",\n        suffix=\".tmp\",\n        dir=str(path.parent),\n    )\n    fd_consumed = False\n    try:\n        fh = os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        fd_consumed = True  # the file object now owns the fd\n        try:\n            json.dump(payload, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)\n            fh.write(\"\\n\")\n        finally:\n            fh.close()\n        os.replace(tmp, path)\n    except Exception:\n        # Two distinct cleanup concerns: an orphaned fd (only when\n        # os.fdopen failed) and an orphaned tmp file (always).\n        if not fd_consumed:\n            try:\n                os.close(fd)\n            except OSError:\n                # Best-effort fd cleanup; the original exception is re-raised\n                # below, so silencing here only suppresses cleanup noise.\n                pass  # nosec B110\n        try:\n            os.unlink(tmp)\n        except OSError:\n            # Best-effort tmp-file cleanup; the original exception is re-raised\n            # below, so silencing here only suppresses cleanup noise.\n            pass  # nosec B110\n        raise\n\n\ndef _atomic_unlink(path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Atomically remove *path* by renaming to a sibling temp first.\n\n    Per D4 cleanup-on-success: a crash mid-delete leaves the cache\n    discoverable under a different name rather than half-deleted.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not path.exists():\n        return\n    tmp = path.with_name(path.name + \".unlinking\")\n    try:\n        os.replace(path, tmp)\n    except OSError:\n        # Best-effort fallback to direct unlink — the cache file may be\n        # gone already (concurrent worker, manual cleanup), and that's fine.\n        try:\n            path.unlink()\n        except OSError:\n            pass  # nosec B110\n        return\n    try:\n        tmp.unlink()\n    except OSError:\n        # The rename succeeded but the orphan unlink failed. build_phase_dispatch_payload(\n    phase: str,\n    change_id: str,\n    provider: str | None = None,\n    agent_id: str | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Return a provider-neutral phase str,\n    phase: str,\n    outcome: str,\n    handoff_id: str,\n    *,\n    allow_phase_mismatch: bool = False,\n    change_dir: Path | None = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Update loop-state.json after a phase sub-agent returns (D4).\n\n    ``change_dir`` (roadmap ri-06): on the non-replay path, when *phase* is\n    ``\"GATEKEEPER\"``, also builds and appends a ``\"GATEKEEPER_SHADOW\"``\n    ``phase_history`` entry via ``gatekeeper_shadow.build_shadow_entry`` --\n    the real host-driven GATEKEEPER dispatch protocol\n    (``skills/autopilot/SKILL.md`` Step 1.5: ``build-dispatch`` /\n    ``apply-outcome``) never calls the Python-level ``_phase_gatekeeper``, so\n    this is the only place a production run can record shadow data (Codex\n    review, PR #591, P1). Replay-safe: the shadow judgment is skipped\n    entirely on the replay path above, so a retried ``apply-outcome`` call\n    never doubles the ``decide()`` call count or the shadow record.\n\n    **No-transition contract (design D1 Layer A / Task 3):** this function\n    updates ONLY the fields it owns — ``last_handoff_id``, ``handoff_ids``\n    (append), ``phase_archetype``, and a new ``phase_history`` entry. It\n    NEVER modifies ``current_phase``. The orchestrator is the sole writer\n    of ``current_phase``.\n\n    **Phase-mismatch guard (Task 3.2-3.4):** on the non-replay path, if\n    *phase* does not equal loop-state's ``current_phase`` the call raises\n    ``ValueError`` (surfaced as a non-zero exit by the runner CLI) unless\n    *allow_phase_mismatch* is set. NOT parameterized — every dispatch in this skill uses this exact\n# string and spec scenarios assert it verbatim.\n_PROMPT_SEPARATOR = \"\\n\\n---\\n\\n\"\n\n# OpenSpec change-id pattern (also enforced by OpenSpec itself). The two have to be tracked\n    separately because `os.fdopen` could (theoretically — extremely\n    rare) raise after `mkstemp` returned, in which case the with-block\n    never owns the fd and we'd leak it without an explicit close.\n    \"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    # nosec B108: dir= confines the tempfile to the target directory (not\n    # /tmp), which is the canonical pattern for atomic same-fs replace.\n    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(  # noqa: S108\n        prefix=path.name + \".\",\n        suffix=\".tmp\",\n        dir=str(path.parent),\n    )\n    fd_consumed = False\n    try:\n        fh = os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        fd_consumed = True  # the file object now owns the fd\n        try:\n            json.dump(payload, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)\n            fh.write(\"\\n\")\n        finally:\n            fh.close()\n        os.replace(tmp, path)\n    except Exception:\n        # Two distinct cleanup concerns: an orphaned fd (only when\n        # os.fdopen failed) and an orphaned tmp file (always).\n        if not fd_consumed:\n            try:\n                os.close(fd)\n            except OSError:\n                # Best-effort fd cleanup; the original exception is re-raised\n                # below, so silencing here only suppresses cleanup noise.\n                pass  # nosec B110\n        try:\n            os.unlink(tmp)\n        except OSError:\n            # Best-effort tmp-file cleanup; build_phase_dispatch_payload(\n    phase: str,\n    change_id: str,\n    provider: str | None = None,\n    agent_id: str | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Return a provider-neutral phase str,\n    phase: str,\n    outcome: str,\n    handoff_id: str,\n    *,\n    allow_phase_mismatch: bool = False,\n    change_dir: Path | None = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Update loop-state.json after a phase sub-agent returns (D4).\n\n    ``change_dir`` (roadmap ri-06): on the non-replay path, when *phase* is\n    ``\"GATEKEEPER\"``, also builds and appends a ``\"GATEKEEPER_SHADOW\"``\n    ``phase_history`` entry via ``gatekeeper_shadow.build_shadow_entry`` --\n    the real host-driven GATEKEEPER dispatch protocol\n    (``skills/autopilot/SKILL.md`` Step 1.5: ``build-dispatch`` /\n    ``apply-outcome``) never calls the Python-level ``_phase_gatekeeper``, so\n    this is the only place a production run can record shadow data (Codex\n    review, PR #591, P1). Replay-safe: the shadow judgment is skipped\n    entirely on the replay path above, so a retried ``apply-outcome`` call\n    never doubles the ``decide()`` call count or the shadow record.\n\n    **No-transition contract (design D1 Layer A / Task 3):** this function\n    updates ONLY the fields it owns — ``last_handoff_id``, ``handoff_ids``\n    (append), ``phase_archetype``, and a new ``phase_history`` entry. It\n    NEVER modifies ``current_phase``. The orchestrator is the sole writer\n    of ``current_phase``.\n\n    **Phase-mismatch guard (Task 3.2-3.4):** on the non-replay path, if\n    *phase* does not equal loop-state's ``current_phase`` the call raises\n    ``ValueError`` (surfaced as a non-zero exit by the runner CLI) unless\n    *allow_phase_mismatch* is set. NOT parameterized — every dispatch in this skill uses this exact\n# string and spec scenarios assert it verbatim.\n_PROMPT_SEPARATOR = \"\\n\\n---\\n\\n\"\n\n# OpenSpec change-id pattern (also enforced by OpenSpec itself). The two have to be tracked\n    separately because `os.fdopen` could (theoretically — extremely\n    rare) raise after `mkstemp` returned, in which case the with-block\n    never owns the fd and we'd leak it without an explicit close.\n    \"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    # nosec B108: dir= confines the tempfile to the target directory (not\n    # /tmp), which is the canonical pattern for atomic same-fs replace.\n    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(  # noqa: S108\n        prefix=path.name + \".\",\n        suffix=\".tmp\",\n        dir=str(path.parent),\n    )\n    fd_consumed = False\n    try:\n        fh = os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        fd_consumed = True  # the file object now owns the fd\n        try:\n            json.dump(payload, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)\n            fh.write(\"\\n\")\n        finally:\n            fh.close()\n        os.replace(tmp, path)\n    except Exception:\n        # Two distinct cleanup concerns: an orphaned fd (only when\n        # os.fdopen failed) and an orphaned tmp file (always).\n        if not fd_consumed:\n            try:\n                os.close(fd)\n            except OSError:\n                # Best-effort fd cleanup; the original exception is re-raised\n                # below, so silencing here only suppresses cleanup noise.\n                pass  # nosec B110\n        try:\n            os.unlink(tmp)\n        except OSError:\n            # Best-effort tmp-file cleanup; the original exception is re-raised\n            # below, so silencing here only suppresses cleanup noise.\n            pass  # nosec B110\n        raise\n\n\ndef _atomic_unlink(path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Atomically remove *path* by renaming to a sibling temp first.\n\n    Per D4 cleanup-on-success: a crash mid-delete leaves the cache\n    discoverable under a different name rather than half-deleted.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not path.exists():\n        return\n    tmp = path.with_name(path.name + \".unlinking\")\n    try:\n        os.replace(path, tmp)\n    except OSError:\n        # Best-effort fallback to direct unlink — the cache file may be\n        # gone already (concurrent worker, manual cleanup), and that's fine.\n        try:\n            path.unlink()\n        except OSError:\n            pass  # nosec B110\n        return\n    try:\n        tmp.unlink()\n    except OSError:\n        # The rename succeeded but the orphan unlink failed. build_phase_dispatch_payload(\n    phase: str,\n    change_id: str,\n    provider: str | None = None,\n    agent_id: str | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Return a provider-neutral phase
