str,\n    phase: str,\n    outcome: str,\n    handoff_id: str,\n    *,\n    allow_phase_mismatch: bool = False,\n    change_dir: Path | None = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Update loop-state.json after a phase sub-agent returns (D4).\n\n    ``change_dir`` (roadmap ri-06): on the non-replay path, when *phase* is\n    ``\"GATEKEEPER\"``, also builds and appends a ``\"GATEKEEPER_SHADOW\"``\n    ``phase_history`` entry via ``gatekeeper_shadow.build_shadow_entry`` --\n    the real host-driven GATEKEEPER dispatch protocol\n    (``skills/autopilot/SKILL.md`` Step 1.5: ``build-dispatch`` /\n    ``apply-outcome``) never calls the Python-level ``_phase_gatekeeper``, so\n    this is the only place a production run can record shadow data (Codex\n    review, PR #591, P1). Replay-safe: the shadow judgment is skipped\n    entirely on the replay path above, so a retried ``apply-outcome`` call\n    never doubles the ``decide()`` call count or the shadow record.\n\n    **No-transition contract (design D1 Layer A / Task 3):** this function\n    updates ONLY the fields it owns — ``last_handoff_id``, ``handoff_ids``\n    (append), ``phase_archetype``, and a new ``phase_history`` entry. It\n    NEVER modifies ``current_phase``. The orchestrator is the sole writer\n    of ``current_phase``.\n\n    **Phase-mismatch guard (Task 3.2-3.4):** on the non-replay path, if\n    *phase* does not equal loop-state's ``current_phase`` the call raises\n    ``ValueError`` (surfaced as a non-zero exit by the runner CLI) unless\n    *allow_phase_mismatch* is set. The two have to be tracked\n    separately because `os.fdopen` could (theoretically — extremely\n    rare) raise after `mkstemp` returned, in which case the with-block\n    never owns the fd and we'd leak it without an explicit close.\n    \"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    # nosec B108: dir= confines the tempfile to the target directory (not\n    # /tmp), which is the canonical pattern for atomic same-fs replace.\n    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(  # noqa: S108\n        prefix=path.name + \".\",\n        suffix=\".tmp\",\n        dir=str(path.parent),\n    )\n    fd_consumed = False\n    try:\n        fh = os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        fd_consumed = True  # the file object now owns the fd\n        try:\n            json.dump(payload, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)\n            fh.write(\"\\n\")\n        finally:\n            fh.close()\n        os.replace(tmp, path)\n    except Exception:\n        # Two distinct cleanup concerns: an orphaned fd (only when\n        # os.fdopen failed) and an orphaned tmp file (always).\n        if not fd_consumed:\n            try:\n                os.close(fd)\n            except OSError:\n                # Best-effort fd cleanup; the original exception is re-raised\n                # below, so silencing here only suppresses cleanup noise.\n                pass  # nosec B110\n        try:\n            os.unlink(tmp)\n        except OSError:\n            # Best-effort tmp-file cleanup; str,\n    phase: str,\n    outcome: str,\n    handoff_id: str,\n    *,\n    allow_phase_mismatch: bool = False,\n    change_dir: Path | None = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Update loop-state.json after a phase sub-agent returns (D4).\n\n    ``change_dir`` (roadmap ri-06): on the non-replay path, when *phase* is\n    ``\"GATEKEEPER\"``, also builds and appends a ``\"GATEKEEPER_SHADOW\"``\n The two have to be tracked\n    separately because `os.fdopen` could (theoretically — extremely\n    rare) raise after `mkstemp` returned, in which case the with-block\n    never owns the fd and we'd leak it without an explicit close.\n    \"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    # nosec B108: dir= confines the tempfile to the target directory (not\n    # /tmp), which is the canonical pattern for atomic same-fs replace.\n    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(  # noqa: S108\n        prefix=path.name + \".\",\n        suffix=\".tmp\",\n        dir=str(path.parent),\n    )\n    fd_consumed = False\n    try:\n        fh = os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        fd_consumed = True  # the file object now owns the fd\n        try:\n            json.dump(payload, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)\n            fh.write(\"\\n\")\n        finally:\n            fh.close()\n        os.replace(tmp, path)\n    except Exception:\n        # Two distinct cleanup concerns: an orphaned fd (only when\n        # os.fdopen failed) and an orphaned tmp file (always).\n        if not fd_consumed:\n            try:\n                os.close(fd)\n            except OSError:\n                # Best-effort fd cleanup; the original exception is re-raised\n                # below, so silencing here only suppresses cleanup noise.\n                pass  # nosec B110\n        try:\n            os.unlink(tmp)\n        except OSError:\n            # Best-effort tmp-file cleanup; the original exception is re-raised\n            # below, so silencing here only suppresses cleanup noise.\n            pass  # nosec B110\n        raise\n\n\ndef _atomic_unlink(path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Atomically remove *path* by renaming to a sibling temp first.\n\n    Per D4 cleanup-on-success: a crash mid-delete leaves the cache\n    discoverable under a different name rather than half-deleted.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not path.exists():\n        return\n    tmp = path.with_name(path.name + \".unlinking\")\n    try:\n        os.replace(path, tmp)\n    except OSError:\n        # Best-effort fallback to direct unlink — the cache file may be\n        # gone already (concurrent worker, manual cleanup), and that's fine.\n        try:\n            path.unlink()\n        except OSError:\n            pass  # nosec B110\n        return\n    try:\n        tmp.unlink()\n    except OSError:\n        # The rename succeeded but the orphan unlink failed. Filesystem\n        # GC or the next _atomic_unlink call will sweep the leftover.\n        pass  # nosec B110\n\n\ndef _hydrate_incoming_handoff(\n    change_id: str,\n    last_handoff_id: str | None,\n    current_phase: str,\n) -> PhaseRecord:\n    \"\"\"Bootstrap a PhaseRecord for the prompt scaffold.\n\n    Cross-process production path can't easily reach back into the\n    coordinator for a structured handoff, so we synthesize a minimal\n    bootstrap record. str,\n    phase: str,\n    outcome: str,\n    handoff_id: str,\n    *,\n    allow_phase_mismatch: bool = False,\n    change_dir: Path | None = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Update loop-state.json after a phase sub-agent returns (D4).\n\n    ``change_dir`` (roadmap ri-06): on the non-replay path, when *phase* is\n    ``\"GATEKEEPER\"``, also builds and appends a ``\"GATEKEEPER_SHADOW\"``\n    ``phase_history`` entry via ``gatekeeper_shadow.build_shadow_entry`` --\n    the real host-driven GATEKEEPER dispatch protocol\n    (``skills/autopilot/SKILL.md`` Step 1.5: ``build-dispatch`` /\n    ``apply-outcome``) never calls the Python-level ``_phase_gatekeeper``, so\n    this is the only place a production run can record shadow data (Codex\n    review, PR #591, P1). Replay-safe: the shadow judgment is skipped\n    entirely on the replay path above, so a retried ``apply-outcome`` call\n    never doubles the ``decide()`` call count or the shadow record.\n\n    **No-transition contract (design D1 Layer A / Task 3):** this function\n    updates ONLY the fields it owns — ``last_handoff_id``, ``handoff_ids``\n    (append), ``phase_archetype``, and a new ``phase_history`` entry. It\n    NEVER modifies ``current_phase``. Add Dispatch Sandbox Enforcement\n\n> Parent roadmap: `dispatch-governance` (`dg-07`)\n> Change ID: `add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement`\n> Prerequisites: dg-02, dg-03, dg-05, and dg-06 are landed\n\n## Why\n\nThe router now chooses an isolation posture and the orchestrator carries that immutable\ndecision to execution, but local vendor CLI processes still run with the host user's OS\nauthority. A `worktree` prevents concurrent agents from sharing one checkout; it does not\nprevent reads outside that checkout, writes elsewhere, or arbitrary egress. The coordinator's\nnetwork policy is likewise advisory because it is checked only by callers that volunteer a\ndomain.\n\ndg-07 closes the local execution gap. A shared local-process backend consumes the exact dg-06\ndecision, renders the coordinator's policy for Anthropic Sandbox Runtime (SRT), and applies the\nresult to every vendor CLI lifecycle command: synchronous invocation, asynchronous submission,\npolling, and the autopilot local-provider harness.\n\n## What Changes\n\n### Immutable execution context\n\nDispatch receives a versioned execution context containing the routing decision identifier,\nexact agent/lane identifier, isolation, dispatch mode, canonical worktree root, and provenance.\nThe enforcement layer never re-runs routing. Standalone review-panel calls that have no routed\ncontext resolve the already-landed dg-05 fallback once from the exact `agents.yaml` lane.\nRouted callers carry the complete context in phase payload v2; every adapter lifecycle method\naccepts that context explicitly instead of reconstructing it from cwd.\n\n### Coordinator-owned network-policy export and audit\n\n`NetworkPolicyService` gains an exact-agent export. It returns the active profile-specific and\nglobal rules, a closed default-deny contract, schema revision, and a deterministic digest.\nRendering is conservative: SRT denies take precedence, so conflicting authored rules may become\nnarrower but never wider. A malformed or unavailable cold-start export renders deny-all; it does\nnot invent destinations.\n\nA narrow sandbox-execution audit endpoint durably and idempotently records applied and degraded\noutcomes. If the coordinator is unavailable, a locked mode-0600 JSONL outbox under the operator's\nXDG state directory is fsynced and retried oldest-first on later calls. An unsandboxed fallback is\nallowed only after either the coordinator event or the durable outbox record succeeds.\n\n### Pure renderer and lifecycle-owning backend\n\n`skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` provides:\n\n- pure, deterministic SRT settings rendering;\n- mode-aware filesystem policy (`review` has no project write roots; write-capable modes are\n  confined to the canonical worktree root; every lane gets an ephemeral vendor-state root);\n- a prepared-command lifecycle that owns a unique mode-0600 settings file, sanitized environment,\n  runtime identity, policy digest, process group, and cleanup;\n- an additive renderer seam for future runtimes.\n\nThe reviewed runtime is `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 on Node >=20.11.0. The repository\npins the package and integrity and never installs it during dispatch. Setup/CI install the pin;\nruntime discovery is explicit absolute override, then the dispatcher's Git-root installation,\nthen unavailable. The runtime is accepted only when package metadata and integrity match. On Linux\nthe preflight also verifies `bubblewrap`, `socat`,\n`ripgrep`, user-namespace capability, architecture/seccomp support, and a real no-op SRT launch.\n\nOfficial runtime sources:\n\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/README.md\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/package.json\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-9gqj-5w7c-vx47\n\n### One local command backend\n\nThe shared backend replaces direct vendor subprocess launches in `CliVendorAdapter` sync submit,\nasync submit and poll paths, and in `autopilot/scripts/provider_dispatch.py`. Poll enforcement\nfailures are collection failures retried to the existing deadline, not terminal remote-task\nfailures. A structural guard\nprevents future vendor CLI subprocess sinks outside the backend. Non-sandbox decisions preserve\nargv, stdin, cwd, timeout, and result behavior.\n\n### Loud, bounded degradation\n\nFail-open is restricted to facts known before a vendor process starts: unsupported OS, missing or\nincompatible pinned runtime, or failed platform capability preflight. Those cases warn, durably\naudit `applied=false`, and run the original command. Unsafe roots, malformed policy, settings\nmaterialization errors, and audit/outbox failures fail closed. Once SRT starts, a timeout or\nunknown failure never triggers an unsandboxed retry because doing so could execute work twice.\n\n## Scope Boundary\n\nThis change protects against accidental or confused local tool behavior after sandbox startup.\nIt does not claim containment of a malicious vendor executable, a compromised runtime, same-user\nraces, damage inside an authorized writable root, or exfiltration through an allowed destination\nsuch as GitHub. It strips proxy and code-injection environment variables required to preserve the\nSRT boundary, but vendor credentials deliberately supplied to a CLI remain readable by that CLI.\nRequest-time secret substitution is dg-08; broader credential brokering and cloud execution remain\nowned by `add-sandboxed-harness-execution`.\n\ndg-03's factual `posture.filesystem` means a per-session workspace exists; it is not a security\nattestation and never satisfies a router request for `sandbox`. Wrapping a local submission CLI\nalso does not imply that a remote worker is sandboxed.\n\n## Approaches Considered\n\n### Shared SRT local-process backend (selected)\n\nOne policy renderer and one lifecycle-owning runner cover every current local CLI sink. It enforces\nthe already-authored isolation and network decisions without creating a second router.\n\n### Vendor-native flags only\n\nRejected. A router-sourced\ncontext requires a non-null decision id. No renderer or backend calls routing or derives a root\nfrom ambient process cwd.\n\nContext producers are explicit:\n\n| Caller | Assignment fields | Execution root |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Routed roadmap/autopilot phase | Copy decision id, agent, isolation, location, and mode from the persisted dg-06 decision into payload v2 | Host adds the validated managed-worktree root |\n| Standalone vendor panel | Resolve exact-lane mode override, then entry isolation, exactly once | Adapter validates its explicit invocation cwd |\n| Autopilot local provider | Consume payload v2 unchanged; no legacy reconstruction | Required in the embedded context |\n\ndg-03 posture is diagnostic evidence only. Its filesystem bit means a per-session workspace, not\ncredential containment; its network bit does not prove equivalence to the active coordinator\npolicy. Neither bit satisfies `isolation=sandbox`.\n\n### D2 — One local process backend, not one list wrapper\n\nAll vendor CLI execution sites call `skills/shared/local_process_backend.py`. The pure renderer in\n`sandbox_profile.py` returns settings and a digest; an impure prepared-command context manager\nvalidates runtime/root/policy and materializes a unique 0600 file. Alternative, quick,\nimplementation, and documentation-shaped commands may write only the strict canonical worktree\nroot. Every sandboxed command receives a backend-owned, per-launch state root used for HOME,\nXDG state/config/cache, and runtime temporary files, so vendor CLIs do not need write access to\nthe operator's home. Read-only credential inputs and required environment credential keys remain\nexplicit per-vendor configuration; no renderer hard-codes them. This\navoids granting one agent write access to shared objects and refs.\nSymlink escapes are rejected/tested; hardlink aliasing is measured and documented as a residual\nsame-user risk rather than overstated as contained.\n\n### D4 — Exact-agent, default-deny network export\n\nThe coordinator exports a snapshot from the exact agent's profile assignment plus global rules.\nThe snapshot uses a closed SRT-compatible hostname plus separately range-checked port grammar,\nexplicit scope and priority, schema revision, and canonical SHA-256 digest. Migration 044 adds\n`updated_at` and an atomic exact-agent export function; `policy_revision` is the maximum included\nrow update timestamp plus row count, while the digest is the canonical content change detector.\nDisabled rules are absent.\n\nSRT's deny-first semantics cannot represent every ordered SQL policy exactly. Rendering therefore\nkeeps every applicable deny and only authored allows; conflicts become narrower. New writes are\nvalidated against the export grammar. Any legacy malformed applicable rule makes the entire export\nunrenderable and therefore deny-all; rules are never silently omitted. An unavailable snapshot\nbecomes deny-all. Remaining required vendor\ncredentials are still readable by the vendor process; dg-08 owns request-time substitution and\nthe downstream sandboxed-harness change owns broader credential brokering.\n\n### D6 — Narrow fail-open with durable evidence\n\nOnly unsupported OS, missing/incompatible pinned runtime, or failed pre-launch capability probe\nmay run the original command. _default_agents_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \"agents.yaml\"\n\n\ndef _default_secrets_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \".secrets.yaml\"\n\n\ndef load_agents_config(\n    path: Path | None = None,\n    *,\n    secrets_path: Path | None = None,\n) -> list[AgentEntry]:\n    \"\"\"Load and validate ``agents.yaml``.\n\n ValueError: On duplicate agent names or duplicate ``profile`` values.\n    \"\"\"\n    if path is None:\n        path = _default_agents_path()\n    if secrets_path is None:\n        secrets_path = _default_secrets_path()\n\n    with open(path) as fh:\n        raw = yaml.safe_load(fh)\n\n    if raw is None:\n        raise ValueError(\"Empty agents.yaml file\")\n\n    validate(instance=raw, schema=AGENTS_SCHEMA)\n\n    secrets = _load_secrets_file(secrets_path)\n    entries: list[AgentEntry] = []\n    seen_names: set[str] = set()\n    #: profile name -> the agent that claimed it, so the second claimant can be\n    #: named in the error.\n    seen_profiles: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    for name, agent_data in raw[\"agents\"].items():\n        if name in seen_names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name in file order, so the last entry silently\n        # overwrites the first one's trust level and operations. An agent could\n        # then be promoted to admin without its own trust_level line changing,\n        # and neither orphan disabling nor the registry invariant check would\n        # notice. One agent, one profile row.\n        profile_name = agent_data[\"profile\"]\n        if profile_name in seen_profiles:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"Duplicate profile: '{profile_name}' is declared by both \"\n                f\"'{seen_profiles[profile_name]}' and '{name}'. Each agent needs \"\n                f\"its own profile, or the later entry silently overwrites the \"\n                f\"earlier one's trust level and operations.\"\n            )\n        seen_profiles[profile_name] = name\n\n        raw_key = agent_data.get(\"api_key\")\n        resolved_key: str | None = None\n        if raw_key:\n            resolved_key = interpolate(raw_key, secrets)\n            # Keep unresolved ${VAR} placeholders so that\n            # _resolve_api_key_from_openbao() can extract the variable\n            # name and fetch the secret from OpenBao at runtime.\n\n        cli_config: CliConfig | None = None\n        raw_cli = agent_data.get(\"cli\")\n        if raw_cli:\n            def _parse_mode(mode_data: dict[str, Any]) -> ModeConfig:\n                poll_config: PollConfig | None = None\n                raw_poll = mode_data.get(\"poll\")\n                if raw_poll:\n                    poll_config = PollConfig(\n      \"interval_seconds\", 30,\n                        ),\n                        timeout_seconds=raw_poll.get(\n                            \"timeout_seconds\", 600,\n                        ),\n _default_agents_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \"agents.yaml\"\n\n\ndef _default_secrets_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \".secrets.yaml\"\n\n\ndef load_agents_config(\n    path: Path | None = None,\n    *,\n    secrets_path: Path | None = None,\n) -> list[AgentEntry]:\n    \"\"\"Load and validate ``agents.yaml``.\n\n ValueError: On duplicate agent names or duplicate ``profile`` values.\n    \"\"\"\n    if path is None:\n        path = _default_agents_path()\n    if secrets_path is None:\n        secrets_path = _default_secrets_path()\n\n    with open(path) as fh:\n        raw = yaml.safe_load(fh)\n\n    if raw is None:\n        raise ValueError(\"Empty agents.yaml file\")\n\n    validate(instance=raw, schema=AGENTS_SCHEMA)\n\n    secrets = _load_secrets_file(secrets_path)\n    entries: list[AgentEntry] = []\n    seen_names: set[str] = set()\n    #: profile name -> the agent that claimed it, so the second claimant can be\n    #: named in the error.\n    seen_profiles: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    for name, agent_data in raw[\"agents\"].items():\n        if name in seen_names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name in file order, so the last entry silently\n        # overwrites the first one's trust level and operations. An agent could\n        # then be promoted to admin without its own trust_level line changing,\n        # and neither orphan disabling nor the registry invariant check would\n        # notice. One agent, one profile row.\n        profile_name = agent_data[\"profile\"]\n        if profile_name in seen_profiles:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"Duplicate profile: '{profile_name}' is declared by both \"\n                f\"'{seen_profiles[profile_name]}' and '{name}'. Each agent needs \"\n                f\"its own profile, or the later entry silently overwrites the \"\n                f\"earlier one's trust level and operations.\"\n            )\n        seen_profiles[profile_name] = name\n\n        raw_key = agent_data.get(\"api_key\")\n        resolved_key: str | None = None\n        if raw_key:\n            resolved_key = interpolate(raw_key, secrets)\n            # Keep unresolved ${VAR} placeholders so that\n            # _resolve_api_key_from_openbao() can extract the variable\n            # name and fetch the secret from OpenBao at runtime.\n\n        cli_config: CliConfig | None = None\n        raw_cli = agent_data.get(\"cli\")\n        if raw_cli:\n            def _parse_mode(mode_data: dict[str, Any]) -> ModeConfig:\n                poll_config: PollConfig | None = None\n                raw_poll = mode_data.get(\"poll\")\n                if raw_poll:\n                    poll_config = PollConfig(\n      \"interval_seconds\", 30,\n                        ),\n                        timeout_seconds=raw_poll.get(\n                            \"timeout_seconds\", 600,\n                        ),\n ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# API key identity generation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # skipping\",\n                _PHASE_MODEL_OVERRIDE_ENV, phase,\n            )\n            continue\n        out[phase] = model\n    return out\n\n\ndef _check_phase_model_override(phase: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the override model for *phase* if set in the env var, else None.\"\"\"\n    overrides = _parse_phase_model_override(os.environ.get(_PHASE_MODEL_OVERRIDE_ENV))\n    return overrides.get(phase)\n\n\ndef _selected_provider(provider: str | None = None) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve the active provider from explicit arg or runtime env.\"\"\"\n    raw = provider or os.environ.get(\"AUTOPILOT_PROVIDER\") or os.environ.get(\"AGENT_TYPE\")\n    if not raw:\n        return None\n    normalized = raw.strip()\n    if normalized == \"claude\":\n        return \"claude_code\"\n    return normalized or None\n\n\ndef _build_options(\n    phase: str,\n    state_dict: dict[str, Any],\n    *,\n    provider: str | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Assemble sub-agent dispatch options for *phase*.\n\n    Resolution order (precedence high → low):\n      1. ``AUTOPILOT_PHASE_MODEL_OVERRIDE`` env var (D8) — sets ``model``\n         only; leaves ``system_prompt`` to the harness default.\n      2. Coordinator archetype resolution (D5) — sets both ``model`` and\n         ``system_prompt`` from the resolved archetype, and records the\n         archetype name in ``state_dict[\"_resolved_archetype\"]`` so\n         ``make_phase_callback`` can propagate it to ``LoopState.phase_archetype``.\n      3. Bridge failure (D9) — leaves ``options`` without ``model`` /\n         ``system_prompt``; the harness default applies; phase still\n         dispatches normally.\n\n    ``isolation=\"worktree\"`` is set independently for phases in\n    :data:`_WORKTREE_PHASES`.\n\n    Mutates *state_dict* by writing ``_resolved_archetype`` only on the\n    archetype-resolution path (path 2). The override path (path 1) does\n    NOT record an archetype because the operator's choice carries no\n    archetype semantics.\n    \"\"\"\n    options: dict[str, Any] = {}\n    if phase in _WORKTREE_PHASES:\n        options[\"isolation\"] = \"worktree\"\n\n    # Path 1: operator override\n    override = _check_phase_model_override(phase)\n    if override:\n        options[\"model\"] = override\n        return options\n\n    # Path 2: coordinator archetype resolution\n    signals = _extract_signals_for_phase(phase, state_dict)\n    selected_provider = _selected_provider(provider)\n    resolved = coordination_bridge.try_resolve_archetype_for_phase(\n        phase,\n        signals,\n        provider=selected_provider,\n    )\n    if resolved is not None:\n        options[\"model\"] = resolved[\"model\"]\n        options[\"system_prompt\"] = resolved[\"system_prompt\"]\n        state_dict[\"_resolved_archetype\"] = resolved[\"archetype\"]\n        # The coordinator rewrites `provider` to the vendor that actually owns\n        # the selected model, because adaptive routing ranks the whole catalog\n        # and may cross vendors. Taking `model` without `provider` produces a\n        # pair no adapter can dispatch -- provider=\"codex\" with\n        # model=\"qwen/qwen3-coder\". Optional passthrough, like write_capable:\n        # older coordinators omit it, and then the static provider stands.\n        if resolved.get(\"provider\"):\n            state_dict[\"_resolved_provider\"] = resolved[\"provider\"]\n        # write_capable is an optional passthrough from the coordinator (older\n        # coordinators may omit it); surface it for build-dispatch metadata.\n        if \"write_capable\" in resolved:\n            state_dict[\"_resolved_write_capable\"] = resolved[\"write_capable\"]\n    # Path 3 (bridge None): leave options untouched. The bridge already\n    # logs a structured warning; no need to double-log here.\n\n    return options\n\n\ndef _build_prompt(\n    phase: str,\n    state_dict: dict[str, Any],\n    incoming_handoff: PhaseRecord,\n    artifacts_manifest: list[str] | None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Assemble the standard sub-agent prompt scaffold.\n\n    Three sections per D6:\n      1. Phase + state context (machine-readable)\n      2. Incoming PhaseRecord JSON (the structured handoff)\n      3. Artifacts manifest (paths the sub-agent should read first)\n    \"\"\"\n    incoming_json = json.dumps(incoming_handoff.to_handoff_payload(), indent=2)\n    state_json = json.dumps(_safe_state_dict(state_dict), indent=2)\n\n    parts = [\n        f\"# Autopilot Phase Sub-Agent — {phase}\",\n        \"\",\n        \"You are running as an autopilot phase sub-agent. The orchestrator — NOT you —\",\n        \"owns every state transition. Editing it directly corrupts the loop.\",\n    ])\n\n\ndef _safe_state_dict(state_dict: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Strip non-serializable values from state_dict so json.dumps succeeds.\"\"\"\n    out: dict[str, Any] = {}\n    for k, v in state_dict.items():\n        try:\n            json.dumps(v)\n        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n            out[k] = repr(v)\n        else:\n            out[k] = v\n    return out\n\n\n# Per spec D6: every non-terminal phase has a _PHASE_TASKS entry. Loading the incoming PhaseRecord from state.last_handoff_id\n         (via incoming_handoff_loader, e.g. a coordinator read_handoff).\n      2. Calling ``run_phase_subagent`` with the assembled prompt scaffold.\n      3. Mutating ``state.last_handoff_id`` and ``state.handoff_ids`` with\n         the returned handoff_id.\n      4. Returning ONLY the outcome string to the driver.\n\n    This realizes Layer 2 — the driver-side LoopState delta after the\n    callback returns is bounded to ``last_handoff_id`` + one new entry in\n    ``handoff_ids``. The sub-agent's transcript stays inside this module.\n\n    Args:\n        phase: Phase id to dispatch (e.g. \"IMPLEMENT\").\n        subagent_runner: Runner that invokes the harness Agent tool.\n        incoming_handoff_loader: ``Callable[[handoff_id | None], PhaseRecord]``\n            used to hydrate the previous phase's record. The default loader\n            constructs an empty bootstrap record when last_handoff_id is None\n            (typical at the very first transition).\n        artifacts_manifest: Optional repo-relative paths to include in the\n            standard prompt scaffold.\n        coordinator_writer: Forwarded to run_phase_subagent for the failure\n            path's phase-failed record.\n\n    Returns:\n        ``(state) -> outcome`` callable suitable for use as\n        ``implement_fn``, ``validate_fn``, or the IMPL_REVIEW phase wrapper\n        in autopilot.run_loop.\n    \"\"\"\n    loader = incoming_handoff_loader or _default_incoming_loader\n\n    def callback(state: Any) -> str:\n        last_id = getattr(state, \"last_handoff_id\", None)\n        incoming = loader(last_id)\n        state_change_id = getattr(state, \"change_id\", None)\n        if incoming.change_id == \"\" and isinstance(state_change_id, str) and state_change_id:\n            incoming.change_id = state_change_id\n\n        state_dict = _state_snapshot(state)\n        outcome, handoff_id = run_phase_subagent(\n            phase=phase,\n            state_dict=state_dict,\n            incoming_handoff=incoming,\n            subagent_runner=subagent_runner,\n            artifacts_manifest=artifacts_manifest,\n            coordinator_writer=coordinator_writer,\n        )\n        # Bounded driver-side state delta — D6\n        state.last_handoff_id = handoff_id\n        if hasattr(state, \"handoff_ids\"):\n            state.handoff_ids.append(handoff_id)\n        # D7: propagate the archetype name resolved by _build_options into\n        # LoopState.phase_archetype for audit/observability. Override path\n        # and bridge-failure path leave _resolved_archetype unset, so we\n        # explicitly null the field for those cases (so downstream\n        # observability surfaces \"default-fallback\" phases).\n        if hasattr(state, \"phase_archetype\"):\n            state.phase_archetype = state_dict.get(\"_resolved_archetype\")\n        return outcome\n\n    return callback\n\n\ndef _default_incoming_loader(handoff_id: str | None) -> PhaseRecord:\n    \"\"\"Bootstrap loader — returns an empty PhaseRecord when no prior handoff.\n\n    Production use should pass a loader that calls ``read_handoff`` against\n    the coordinator (or reads the local fallback file) and returns a\n    hydrated PhaseRecord. This default exists so make_phase_callback works\n    in tests without coordinator access.\n    \"\"\"\n    return PhaseRecord(\n        change_id=\"\",\n        phase_name=\"bootstrap\",\n        agent_type=\"autopilot\",\n        summary=(\n            f\"No incoming handoff (last_handoff_id={handoff_id!r}). \"\n            \"Bootstrap phase entry.\"\n        ),\n    )\n\n\ndef _state_snapshot(state: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Extract a serializable snapshot of LoopState for the sub-agent prompt.\n\n    Pulls only fields the sub-agent actually needs to reason about the\n    phase. The sub-agent gets its work-context from the incoming handoff\n    and on-disk artifacts, not from the LoopState directly — keeping the\n    snapshot small reduces prompt-size pressure.\n    \"\"\"\n    fields_of_interest = (\n        \"change_id\",\n        \"current_phase\",\n        \"iteration\",\n        \"total_iterations\",\n        \"max_phase_iterations\",\n        \"findings_trend\",\n        \"previous_phase\",\n    )\n    out: dict[str, Any] = {}\n    for name in fields_of_interest:\n        if hasattr(state, name):\n            out[name] = getattr(state, name)\n    return out\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Production-path helpers (wire-autopilot-phase-subagents)\n#\n# These two functions form the prose↔Python boundary used by SKILL.md per\n# design D1/D2/D3/D4. They are invoked across separate process invocations\n# (one for build-dispatch, one for apply-outcome), so all state lives on\n# disk in `loop-state.json` plus a tiny per-run cache file.\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n# Fixed separator used to fold `system_prompt` into the dispatched prompt\n# (D2). NOT parameterized — every dispatch in this skill uses this exact\n# string and spec scenarios assert it verbatim.\n_PROMPT_SEPARATOR = \"\\n\\n---\\n\\n\"\n\n# OpenSpec change-id pattern (also enforced by OpenSpec itself). Rejects\n# `..`, `/`, empty strings, oversized values, and non-ASCII characters\n# before any path is constructed.\n_CHANGE_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$\")\n\n# Filename of the per-run resolution cache, written by build-dispatch and\n# consumed (then deleted) by apply-outcome. All attempts exhausted — write phase-failed record and raise (D8)\n    _write_phase_failed_record(\n        phase=phase,\n        state_dict=state_dict,\n        incoming_handoff=incoming_handoff,\n        attempts=max_attempts,\n        last_error=last_error,\n        coordinator_writer=coordinator_writer,\n    )\n    raise PhaseEscalationError(phase, max_attempts, last_error)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Prompt + options assembly\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _extract_signals_for_phase(phase: str, state_dict: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Lift the per-phase signal keys from *state_dict*.\n\n    Returns a dict containing only those keys listed in\n    :data:`_PHASE_SIGNAL_KEYS` for *phase* and present in *state_dict*.\n    Missing keys are silently dropped (per spec D12). Unknown phases get\n    an empty dict — they pass no signals and the coordinator falls back\n    to the archetype default model.\n    \"\"\"\n    keys = _PHASE_SIGNAL_KEYS.get(phase, [])\n    return {k: state_dict[k] for k in keys if k in state_dict}\n\n\ndef _parse_phase_model_override(raw: str | None) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Parse ``AUTOPILOT_PHASE_MODEL_OVERRIDE`` into ``{phase: model}``.\n\n    Format: ``<PHASE>=<model>[,<PHASE>=<model>]*``. Whitespace around\n    keys/values is tolerated. Per spec D8:\n\n    - Empty input returns ``{}``.\n    - Entries missing ``=`` are warned and skipped.\n    - Unknown phase names (not in :data:`_PHASE_SIGNAL_KEYS`) are warned\n      and skipped — typo protection.\n    - Empty model values are warned and skipped.\n    - Unknown model names pass through (validated downstream by the harness).\n    \"\"\"\n    if not raw or not raw.strip():\n        return {}\n    out: dict[str, str] = {}\n    for entry in raw.split(\",\"):\n        entry = entry.strip()\n        if not entry:\n            continue\n        if \"=\" not in entry:\n            logger.warning(\n                \"%s: malformed entry %r (missing '='); skipping\",\n                _PHASE_MODEL_OVERRIDE_ENV, entry,\n            )\n            continue\n        phase, model = entry.split(\"=\", 1)\n        phase = phase.strip()\n        model = model.strip()\n        if phase not in _PHASE_SIGNAL_KEYS:\n            logger.warning(\n                \"%s: unknown phase %r; skipping (known phases: %s)\",\n                _PHASE_MODEL_OVERRIDE_ENV, phase, sorted(_PHASE_SIGNAL_KEYS.keys()),\n            )\n            continue\n        if not model:\n            logger.warning(\n                \"%s: empty model for phase %r; skipping\",\n                _PHASE_MODEL_OVERRIDE_ENV, phase,\n            )\n            continue\n        out[phase] = model\n    return out\n\n\ndef _check_phase_model_override(phase: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the override model for *phase* if set in the env var, else None.\"\"\"\n    overrides = _parse_phase_model_override(os.environ.get(_PHASE_MODEL_OVERRIDE_ENV))\n    return overrides.get(phase)\n\n\ndef _selected_provider(provider: str | None = None) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve the active provider from explicit arg or runtime env.\"\"\"\n    raw = provider or os.environ.get(\"AUTOPILOT_PROVIDER\") or os.environ.get(\"AGENT_TYPE\")\n    if not raw:\n        return None\n    normalized = raw.strip()\n    if normalized == \"claude\":\n        return \"claude_code\"\n    return normalized or None\n\n\ndef _build_options(\n    phase: str,\n    state_dict: dict[str, Any],\n    *,\n    provider: str | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Assemble sub-agent dispatch options for *phase*.\n\n    Resolution order (precedence high → low):\n      1. ``AUTOPILOT_PHASE_MODEL_OVERRIDE`` env var (D8) — sets ``model``\n         only; leaves ``system_prompt`` to the harness default.\n      2. Coordinator archetype resolution (D5) — sets both ``model`` and\n         ``system_prompt`` from the resolved archetype, and records the\n         archetype name in ``state_dict[\"_resolved_archetype\"]`` so\n         ``make_phase_callback`` can propagate it to ``LoopState.phase_archetype``.\n      3. Bridge failure (D9) — leaves ``options`` without ``model`` /\n         ``system_prompt``; the harness default applies; phase still\n         dispatches normally.\n\n    ``isolation=\"worktree\"`` is set independently for phases in\n    :data:`_WORKTREE_PHASES`.\n\n    Mutates *state_dict* by writing ``_resolved_archetype`` only on the\n    archetype-resolution path (path 2). The override path (path 1) does\n    NOT record an archetype because the operator's choice carries no\n    archetype semantics.\n    \"\"\"\n    options: dict[str, Any] = {}\n    if phase in _WORKTREE_PHASES:\n        options[\"isolation\"] = \"worktree\"\n\n    # Path 1: operator override\n    override = _check_phase_model_override(phase)\n    if override:\n        options[\"model\"] = override\n        return options\n\n    # Path 2: coordinator archetype resolution\n    signals = _extract_signals_for_phase(phase, state_dict)\n    selected_provider = _selected_provider(provider)\n    resolved = coordination_bridge.try_resolve_archetype_for_phase(\n        phase,\n        signals,\n        provider=selected_provider,\n    )\n    if resolved is not None:\n        options[\"model\"] = resolved[\"model\"]\n        options[\"system_prompt\"] = resolved[\"system_prompt\"]\n        state_dict[\"_resolved_archetype\"] = resolved[\"archetype\"]\n        # The coordinator rewrites `provider` to the vendor that actually owns\n        # the selected model, because adaptive routing ranks the whole catalog\n        # and may cross vendors. Taking `model` without `provider` produces a\n        # pair no adapter can dispatch -- provider=\"codex\" with\n        # model=\"qwen/qwen3-coder\". Optional passthrough, like write_capable:\n        # older coordinators omit it, and then the static provider stands.\n        if resolved.get(\"provider\"):\n            state_dict[\"_resolved_provider\"] = resolved[\"provider\"]\n        # write_capable is an optional passthrough from the coordinator (older\n        # coordinators may omit it); surface it for build-dispatch metadata.\n        if \"write_capable\" in resolved:\n            state_dict[\"_resolved_write_capable\"] = resolved[\"write_capable\"]\n    # Path 3 (bridge None): leave options untouched. The bridge already\n    # logs a structured warning; no need to double-log here.\n\n    return options\n\n\ndef _build_prompt(\n    phase: str,\n    state_dict: dict[str, Any],\n    incoming_handoff: PhaseRecord,\n    artifacts_manifest: list[str] | None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Assemble the standard sub-agent prompt scaffold.\n\n    Three sections per D6:\n      1. Phase + state context (machine-readable)\n      2. Incoming PhaseRecord JSON (the structured handoff)\n      3. Artifacts manifest (paths the sub-agent should read first)\n    \"\"\"\n    incoming_json = json.dumps(incoming_handoff.to_handoff_payload(), indent=2)\n    state_json = json.dumps(_safe_state_dict(state_dict), indent=2)\n\n    parts = [\n        f\"# Autopilot Phase Sub-Agent — {phase}\",\n        \"\",\n        \"You are running as an autopilot phase sub-agent. Return exactly\",\n        \"(outcome, handoff_id) when complete. Do not surface intermediate state.\",\n        \"\",\n        \"## Phase Context\",\n        \"\",\n        \"```json\",\n        state_json,\n        \"```\",\n        \"\",\n        \"## Incoming Handoff (previous phase's PhaseRecord)\",\n        \"\",\n        \"```json\",\n        incoming_json,\n        \"```\",\n        \"\",\n    ]\n    if artifacts_manifest:\n        parts.append(\"## Artifacts Manifest\")\n        parts.append(\"\")\n        for path in artifacts_manifest:\n            parts.append(f\"- {path}\")\n        parts.append(\"\")\n    parts.append(\"## Phase Task\")\n    parts.append(\"\")\n    parts.append(_phase_task_instructions(phase))\n    prohibitions = _state_mutation_prohibitions(phase, state_dict)\n    if prohibitions:\n        parts.append(\"\")\n        parts.append(prohibitions)\n    return \"\\n\".join(parts)\n\n\n# Write-capable phases must carry the state-mutation prohibitions (Layers B+C).\n# This set is exactly the write-capable phase list from design D7 and mirrors\n# _WORKTREE_PHASES. State-only phases (INIT, SUBMIT_PR) and the read-only\n# GATEKEEPER judge are intentionally excluded.\n_STATE_MUTATION_PROHIBITION_PHASES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(_WORKTREE_PHASES)\n\n\ndef _state_mutation_prohibitions(phase: str, state_dict: dict[str, Any]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the Layer B + Layer C state-mutation prohibition block for *phase*.\n\n    Write-capable phases append two explicit prohibitions to the dispatch\n    prompt (design D1 Layers B + C):\n\n      - Layer B: the sub-agent MUST NOT run ``runner.py apply-outcome`` (or any\n        other runner.py subcommand that mutates orchestrator state).\n      - Layer C: the sub-agent MUST NOT edit ``loop-state.json`` by any means\n        (python3 -c, sed, jq, or any other shell tool).\n\n    Read-only / state-only phases get an empty string (no prohibition needed).\n    \"\"\"\n    if phase not in _STATE_MUTATION_PROHIBITION_PHASES:\n        return \"\"\n    change_id = state_dict.get(\"change_id\")\n    loop_state_path = (\n        f\"openspec/changes/{change_id}/loop-state.json\"\n        if isinstance(change_id, str) and change_id\n        else \"openspec/changes/<id>/loop-state.json\"\n    )\n    return \"\\n\".join([\n        \"## Orchestrator State Ownership (do not violate)\",\n        \"\",\n        \"You return `(outcome, handoff_id)` and exit. The orchestrator — NOT you —\",\n        \"owns every state transition. Specifically:\",\n        \"\",\n        \"- DO NOT run `runner.py apply-outcome` or any other `runner.py` subcommand\",\n        \"  that modifies orchestrator state. The orchestrator runs apply-outcome\",\n        \"  after you return.\",\n        f\"- DO NOT edit `{loop_state_path}` by any means (python3 -c, sed, jq, or any\",\n        \"  other shell tool). The orchestrator owns this file, including\",\n        \"  `current_phase`. Editing it directly corrupts the loop.\",\n    ])\n\n\ndef _safe_state_dict(state_dict: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Strip non-serializable values from state_dict so json.dumps succeeds.\"\"\"\n    out: dict[str, Any] = {}\n    for k, v in state_dict.items():\n        try:\n            json.dumps(v)\n        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n            out[k] = repr(v)\n        else:\n            out[k] = v\n    return out\n\n\n# Per spec D6: every non-terminal phase has a _PHASE_TASKS entry. State-only\n# phases (INIT, SUBMIT_PR per D13) use a None sentinel — they record their\n# resolved archetype for audit (via the autopilot driver) but do not dispatch\n# a sub-agent.\n_PHASE_TASKS: dict[str, str | None] = {\n    \"INIT\": None,  # D13: state-only — no sub-agent dispatch\n    \"GATEKEEPER\": (\n        \"You are the autopilot gatekeeper. VERIFIABILITY — can the intended outcomes be objectively checked?\\n\"\n        \"     Inspect state.gate_signals (has_specs, has_tasks, has_proposal,\\n\"\n        \"     has_work_packages) and the artifacts themselves. WHEN/THEN specs,\\n\"\n        \"     a task breakdown, and testable acceptance criteria make outcomes\\n\"\n        \"     verifiable; a vague description does not.\\n\"\n        \"  2. RISK — what is the blast radius and reversibility if a slice goes\\n\"\n        \"     wrong? Weigh has_db_migration, has_security_signal,\\n\"\n        \"     external_dep_count, and write scope.\\n\"\n        \"Account for autopilot's downstream safeguards: multi-vendor PLAN/IMPL\\n\"\n        \"review convergence, the VALIDATE phase, and a MANDATORY human merge\\n\"\n        \"gate (nothing reaches main without operator approval). Bias toward\\n\"\n        \"letting verifiable work proceed — large but well-specified changes are\\n\"\n        \"fine. Reserve escalation for work whose outcomes cannot be verified or\\n\"\n        \"whose risk is high AND hard to reverse.\\n\"\n        \"Return outcome 'proceed' for verifiable, acceptable-risk work;\\n\"\n        \"'proceed_with_review' to also enable the extra VAL_REVIEW phase; or\\n\"\n        \"'escalate' to stop for a human when outcomes are unverifiable or the\\n\"\n        \"risk is unacceptable.\"\n    ),\n    \"PLAN\": (\n        \"Run /plan-feature for the change described in state.change_id.\\n\"\n        \"Produce proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md, work-packages.yaml, and\\n\"\n        \"specs/. Return outcome 'created' (or 'exists' if already present),\\n\"\n        \"'failed' on unrecoverable error.\"\n    ),\n    \"PLAN_ITERATE\": (\n        \"Run /iterate-on-plan for state.change_id. Refine the proposal\\n\"\n        \"across completeness, clarity, feasibility, scope, consistency,\\n\"\n        \"testability, parallelizability, and assumptions axes. Return\\n\"\n        \"outcome 'complete' when refinements settle, 'failed' otherwise.\"\n    ),\n    \"PLAN_REVIEW\": (\n        \"Run converge() from skills/autopilot/scripts/convergence_loop.py\\n\"\n        \"as the whole PLAN_REVIEW phase for state.change_id. Do NOT run\\n\"\n        \"/parallel-review-plan as a one-shot cold review. Pass a real\\n\"\n        \"PLAN_FIX applicator as fix_callback (inline edits of cited\\n\"\n        \"file_paths only) and record PLAN_FIX as a phase_history sub-step\\n\"\n        \"around that operation. Do not return 'not_converged' to bounce the outer machine\\n\"\n        \"into PLAN_FIX.\"\n    ),\n    \"PLAN_FIX\": (\n        \"PLAN_FIX is the inner fix_callback of converge(), not an outer\\n\"\n        \"cold-review bounce. Apply blocking ledger items by editing only\\n\"\n        \"their cited file_paths (proposal.md, design.md, specs,\\n\"\n        \"work-packages.yaml). Return outcome 'fixed' on success, 'stuck'\\n\"\n        \"if findings cannot be resolved within the budget.\"\n    ),\n    \"IMPLEMENT\": (\n        \"Implement the next slice of work per tasks.md. Commit per task.\\n\"\n        \"Your starting checkout is a disposable launchpad: it is EXPECTED to\\n\"\n        \"be rooted at main with no change directory and is not the workspace.\\n\"\n        \"Start by running /implement-feature so worktree.py can adopt the\\n\"\n        \"resolved feature parent branch and re-root you into the managed\\n\"\n        \"agent worktree — do all work and commits there. Do not merge the\\n\"\n        \"feature branch into a harness/default-branch checkout to get\\n\"\n        \"context; abort if branch adoption fails. Push commits to the feature\\n\"\n        \"branch. Return outcome 'complete' on success, 'failed' on\\n\"\n        \"unrecoverable error.\"\n    ),\n    \"IMPL_ITERATE\": (\n        \"Run /iterate-on-implementation for state.change_id. Refine the\\n\"\n        \"implementation by fixing bugs, edge cases, and quality issues.\\n\"\n        \"Return outcome 'complete' when refinements settle, 'failed' otherwise.\"\n    ),\n    \"IMPL_REVIEW\": (\n        \"Run converge() from skills/autopilot/scripts/convergence_loop.py\\n\"\n        \"as the whole IMPL_REVIEW phase for state.change_id (fix_mode=\\n\"\n        \"targeted). Return outcome 'fixed' on\\n\"\n        \"success, 'stuck' if findings cannot be resolved within budget.\"\n    ),\n    \"VALIDATE\": (\n        \"Run validation phases (spec, evidence, deploy, smoke, security,\\n\"\n        \"e2e) per validate-feature. Do NOT dispatch a one-shot\\n\"\n        \"cold validation review. Pass a real VAL_FIX applicator as\\n\"\n        \"fix_callback and record VAL_FIX as a phase_history sub-step.\\n\"\n        \"Return 'converged' if validation passes critique, 'max_iter'\\n\"\n        \"otherwise.\"\n    ),\n    \"VAL_FIX\": (\n        \"VAL_FIX is the inner fix_callback of converge(), not an outer\\n\"\n        \"cold-review bounce. Return\\n\"\n        \"outcome 'fixed' on success, 'stuck' otherwise.\"\n    ),\n    \"SUBMIT_PR\": None,  # D13: state-only — no sub-agent dispatch\n}\n\n\ndef _phase_task_instructions(phase: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the task instruction string for *phase*.\n\n    Falls back to a generic execute-and-report instruction for unknown\n    phases (backward-compat with phase strings outside the registered\n    13 non-terminal phases). State-only phases (None sentinel) get a\n    short audit-only instruction; they should not be reaching this\n    function under normal autopilot dispatch.\n    \"\"\"\n    entry = _PHASE_TASKS.get(phase)\n    if entry is None:\n        if phase in _PHASE_TASKS:\n            # State-only sentinel — emit a short audit-only instruction.\n            return (\n                f\"Phase {phase} is a state-only transition. No sub-agent work.\\n\"\n                \"Return ('continue', '<audit-only-handoff-id>').\"\n            )\n        return f\"Execute phase {phase}. Return (outcome, handoff_id) on completion.\"\n    return entry\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Result validation\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _validate_result(result: Any) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:\n    \"\"\"Return (outcome, handoff_id) if shape matches, else (None, None).\"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(result, tuple) or len(result) != 2:\n        return None, None\n    outcome, handoff_id = result\n    if not isinstance(outcome, str) or not outcome:\n        return None, None\n    if not isinstance(handoff_id, str) or not handoff_id:\n        return None, None\n    return outcome, handoff_id\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Failure path\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _write_phase_failed_record(\n    *,\n    phase: str,\n    state_dict: dict[str, Any],\n    incoming_handoff: PhaseRecord,\n    attempts: int,\n    last_error: str,\n    coordinator_writer: Any,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Record a phase-failed PhaseRecord before raising PhaseEscalationError.\n\n    Best-effort: failures inside this routine log a warning but do not\n    suppress the escalation.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        change_id = state_dict.get(\"change_id\") or incoming_handoff.change_id\n        record = PhaseRecord(\n            change_id=change_id,\n            phase_name=f\"{phase} (failed)\",\n            agent_type=\"autopilot\",\n            summary=(\n                f\"Phase {phase} sub-agent failed after {attempts} attempts. \"\n                f\"Last error: {last_error}\"\n            ),\n            open_questions=[\n                f\"Why did {phase} fail repeatedly?\",\n                \"Is the incoming handoff stale or malformed?\",\n            ],\n        )\n        record.write_both(coordinator_writer=coordinator_writer)\n    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001\n        logger.warning(\n            \"phase_agent: writing phase-failed record raised: %s\", exc,\n        )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Driver-facing wiring helper\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef make_phase_callback(\n    *,\n    phase: str,\n    subagent_runner: SubagentRunner,\n    incoming_handoff_loader: Callable[[str | None], PhaseRecord] | None = None,\n    artifacts_manifest: list[str] | None = None,\n    coordinator_writer: Any = None,\n) -> Callable[[Any], str]:\n    \"\"\"Produce an autopilot-compatible phase callback wrapping run_phase_subagent.\n\n    The returned callback matches autopilot's existing callback signature\n    ``(state) -> outcome`` while internally:\n      1. Loading the incoming PhaseRecord from state.last_handoff_id\n         (via incoming_handoff_loader, e.g. a coordinator read_handoff).\n      2. Calling ``run_phase_subagent`` with the assembled prompt scaffold.\n      3. Mutating ``state.last_handoff_id`` and ``state.handoff_ids`` with\n         the returned handoff_id.\n      4. Returning ONLY the outcome string to the driver.\n\n    This realizes Layer 2 — the driver-side LoopState delta after the\n    callback returns is bounded to ``last_handoff_id`` + one new entry in\n    ``handoff_ids``. The sub-agent's transcript stays inside this module.\n\n    Args:\n        phase: Phase id to dispatch (e.g. \"IMPLEMENT\").\n        subagent_runner: Runner that invokes the harness Agent tool.\n        incoming_handoff_loader: ``Callable[[handoff_id | None], PhaseRecord]``\n            used to hydrate the previous phase's record. The default loader\n            constructs an empty bootstrap record when last_handoff_id is None\n            (typical at the very first transition).\n        artifacts_manifest: Optional repo-relative paths to include in the\n            standard prompt scaffold.\n        coordinator_writer: Forwarded to run_phase_subagent for the failure\n            path's phase-failed record.\n\n    Returns:\n        ``(state) -> outcome`` callable suitable for use as\n        ``implement_fn``, ``validate_fn``, or the IMPL_REVIEW phase wrapper\n        in autopilot.run_loop.\n    \"\"\"\n    loader = incoming_handoff_loader or _default_incoming_loader\n\n    def callback(state: Any) -> str:\n        last_id = getattr(state, \"last_handoff_id\", None)\n        incoming = loader(last_id)\n        state_change_id = getattr(state, \"change_id\", None)\n        if incoming.change_id == \"\" and isinstance(state_change_id, str) and state_change_id:\n            incoming.change_id = state_change_id\n\n        state_dict = _state_snapshot(state)\n        outcome, handoff_id = run_phase_subagent(\n            phase=phase,\n            state_dict=state_dict,\n            incoming_handoff=incoming,\n            subagent_runner=subagent_runner,\n            artifacts_manifest=artifacts_manifest,\n            coordinator_writer=coordinator_writer,\n        )\n        # Bounded driver-side state delta — D6\n        state.last_handoff_id = handoff_id\n        if hasattr(state, \"handoff_ids\"):\n            state.handoff_ids.append(handoff_id)\n        # D7: propagate the archetype name resolved by _build_options into\n        # LoopState.phase_archetype for audit/observability. Override path\n        # and bridge-failure path leave _resolved_archetype unset, so we\n        # explicitly null the field for those cases (so downstream\n        # observability surfaces \"default-fallback\" phases).\n        if hasattr(state, \"phase_archetype\"):\n            state.phase_archetype = state_dict.get(\"_resolved_archetype\")\n        return outcome\n\n    return callback\n\n\ndef _default_incoming_loader(handoff_id: str | None) -> PhaseRecord:\n    \"\"\"Bootstrap loader — returns an empty PhaseRecord when no prior handoff.\n\n    Production use should pass a loader that calls ``read_handoff`` against\n    the coordinator (or reads the local fallback file) and returns a\n    hydrated PhaseRecord. This default exists so make_phase_callback works\n    in tests without coordinator access.\n    \"\"\"\n    return PhaseRecord(\n        change_id=\"\",\n        phase_name=\"bootstrap\",\n        agent_type=\"autopilot\",\n        summary=(\n            f\"No incoming handoff (last_handoff_id={handoff_id!r}). \"\n            \"Bootstrap phase entry.\"\n        ),\n    )\n\n\ndef _state_snapshot(state: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Extract a serializable snapshot of LoopState for the sub-agent prompt.\n\n    Pulls only fields the sub-agent actually needs to reason about the\n    phase. The sub-agent gets its work-context from the incoming handoff\n    and on-disk artifacts, not from the LoopState directly — keeping the\n    snapshot small reduces prompt-size pressure.\n    \"\"\"\n    fields_of_interest = (\n        \"change_id\",\n        \"current_phase\",\n        \"iteration\",\n        \"total_iterations\",\n        \"max_phase_iterations\",\n        \"findings_trend\",\n        \"previous_phase\",\n    )\n    out: dict[str, Any] = {}\n    for name in fields_of_interest:\n        if hasattr(state, name):\n            out[name] = getattr(state, name)\n    return out\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Production-path helpers (wire-autopilot-phase-subagents)\n#\n# These two functions form the prose↔Python boundary used by SKILL.md per\n# design D1/D2/D3/D4. They are invoked across separate process invocations\n# (one for build-dispatch, one for apply-outcome), so all state lives on\n# disk in `loop-state.json` plus a tiny per-run cache file.\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n# Fixed separator used to fold `system_prompt` into the dispatched prompt\n# (D2). NOT parameterized — every dispatch in this skill uses this exact\n# string and spec scenarios assert it verbatim.\n_PROMPT_SEPARATOR = \"\\n\\n---\\n\\n\"\n\n# OpenSpec change-id pattern (also enforced by OpenSpec itself).
